title: Performance Engineer, Kernels
description:
PERFORMANCE ENGINEER, KERNELS

Part of Sarvam's Performance Engineering team. We are hiring two specialized performance roles - Kernels (this posting) and Inference (companion posting). They are a vertical stack: the kernels team authors the µs-level GPU code, and the inference team integrates it into a running serving stack and owns the system-level numbers. If your depth genuinely spans both, apply to either and tell us - but most candidates are strongest in one, and we hire for that depth.



Location: [Bengaluru / Chennai / Hybrid / On-site]  ·  Team: Performance Engineering  ·  Level: Senior




ABOUT THE TEAM

Sarvam serves multiple model families - small and large LLMs, Mixture-of-Experts, streaming Indic ASR, and multimodal - across a multi-node, multi-tenant fleet on H100 / H200 / B200. The Performance Engineering team owns the numbers the rest of the company plans against: how fast we serve, how much it costs, and how much we get out of every GPU. This team works at the intersection of the serving runtime, the kernel layer, and the SRE org that keeps the fleet alive.



ABOUT THE ROLE

You will own the kernel layer. Where stock libraries - cuBLAS, cuDNN, FlashAttention, out-of-the-box Triton - leave performance on the table, you will author the custom CUDA, DSL-based, and PTX kernels that close the gap.



This is a hard, narrow, high-leverage role. We hire engineers who have shipped kernels that beat published baselines on real workloads, not engineers who have used kernels. When your code lands, production p99 moves, and you own the explanation of why.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years in ML systems, with 2+ years authoring production CUDA kernels. You have a kernel in production that beat the prior baseline by a measurable margin.

 - CUDA at kernel-authoring level: thread-block sizing, shared-memory layout, warp primitives, async copies (cp.async, TMA), and MMA selection.

 - CUTLASS / CuTe DSL at a modify-and-extend level, with comfort in the layout algebra.

 - PTX at a debug-and-modify level - you have inserted hand-written PTX where the compiler missed.

 - Nsight Compute and Systems fluency: you read a roofline plot and propose the fix.

 - Attention kernels: you have authored or modified at least one (FlashAttention-family, paged, MLA, sliding-window, or sparse).

 - Multi-architecture awareness: what changes from Hopper to Blackwell (TMA, WGMMA, tcgen05).



STRONG PLUSES

 - Communication kernels - NCCL / NVSHMEM authoring, custom collectives, expert-parallel dispatch (DeepEP-style), AFD bipartite comms (StepMesh-style), KV transfer (DualPath / Mooncake). Strongly desired; dedicated comms-specialist headcount is expected later.

 - Open-source kernel contributions - FlashAttention, CUTLASS examples, vLLM / SGLang kernels, DeepEP, Mooncake, or non-trivial Triton work. For this role, the GitHub filter is the highest-yield signal.

 - tcgen05, TMA, CTA-cluster launch and distributed shared memory, async pipelining, and the FP4/microscaling paths

 - Grace-side host-path optimization on GH200 / GB200.

title: Performance Engineer, Inference
description:
PERFORMANCE ENGINEER, INFERENCE

Part of Sarvam's Performance Engineering team. We are hiring two specialized performance roles - Inference (this posting) and Kernels (companion posting). They are a vertical stack: the kernels team authors the µs-level GPU code, and the inference team integrates it into a running serving stack and owns the system-level numbers. If your depth genuinely spans both, apply to either and tell us - but most candidates are strongest in one, and we hire for that depth.



Location: [Bengaluru / Chennai / Hybrid / On-site]  ·  Team: Performance Engineering  ·  Level: Senior




ABOUT THE TEAM

Sarvam serves multiple model families - small and large LLMs, Mixture-of-Experts, Indic ASR & TTS, streaming models and multimodal models - across a multi-node, multi-tenant fleet of Hoppers and Blackwells. The Performance Engineering team owns the numbers the rest of the company plans against: how fast we serve, how much it costs, and how much we get out of every GPU. This team works at the intersection of the serving runtime, the kernel layer, and the SRE org that keeps the fleet alive.


ABOUT THE ROLE

You will own Sarvam's production serving path for large distributed models end to end. You should be source-level fluent in at least one of SGLang, vLLM, NVIDIA Dynamo, or TensorRT-LLM - able to read and modify it where stock behavior does not fit our workloads - and you should operate and extend a distributed-serving stack at depth: disaggregated prefill-decode across nodes, distributed KV/cache transfer, and the routing and scheduling that span them. You will integrate artifacts from the model and kernel teams into a running multi-node, multi-tenant stack, and you will build and train your own speculators - draft models, distillation from the target, acceptance-rate tuning against the live serving distribution - rather than only wiring in stock implementations. You will produce, and defend, the latency and throughput numbers the company plans against, and you will spend significant time in cross-team work with architecture co-design, the kernels team, the model team, and SRE.


Your scoreboard: TTFT (p50 / p95 / p99), TPOT, throughput, GPU utilization, and cost per million tokens.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years in ML systems, with 2+ years on inference serving at production scale. Your record shows concrete outcomes - tokens per day, throughput wins, p99 reductions - rather than "deployed a model."

 - Experience serving 100B+ parameter models in production across multi-node tensor, pipeline, or expert parallelism.

 - Source-level fluency in one of SGLang, vLLM, Dynamo, or TensorRT-LLM - you have modified the scheduler, the KV allocator, or the disaggregation path - and reading-level familiarity with the other three.

 - Distributed serving at operating-and-extending depth: a disaggregated prefill-decode stack, distributed KV/cache transfer (Mooncake or equivalent), and cross-node routing and scheduling. You have run one of these in production and modified it where it didn't fit.

 - Speculative decoding as a build-and-train competency: you have trained your own draft models or speculators (EAGLE / DFlash or otherwise), distilled them from a target model, measured and tuned acceptance rate against a real serving distribution, and composed speculation with the rest of the stack - not only integrated a stock implementation.

 - Deep understanding of KV cache internals: block tables, copy-on-write, prefix sharing, and fragmentation.

 - Working command of TP / PP / EP, NCCL primitives, and how they interact with the scheduler.

 - Multi-tenant serving: model co-location and MIG / MPS isolation.

 - Profiling fluency with Nsight Systems, framework tracing, and py-spy / perf.

 - C++ and CUDA at a read-and-modify level.

 - On-call ownership of an inference SLO.


STRONG PLUSES

 - Upstream contributions to SGLang, vLLM, Dynamo, llm-d, TensorRT-LLM, or LMDeploy on non-trivial code paths.

 - Direct production experience with Dynamo or llm-d at scale.

 - Having operated a forked runtime in production.

 - Published or shipped speculator work - a draft model or speculative-decoding technique you trained and measured.

 - MoE serving at scale, long-context (128K+), multi-model serving, or Indic and multilingual workloads.

title: Deployment Strategist
description:
India's largest banks, insurers, digital natives and government departments are not short of AI pilots. They are short of AI in production.

Closing that gap is the hardest problem in enterprise AI, and it is what Deployment Strategists at Sarvam do. You own the arc of a customer engagement, from the first proof of concept through to their systems running live, handling millions of real conversations across Indian languages and delivering the outcomes we signed up to. If Sarvam's technology is going to reach a billion people rather than sit in a slide deck, it happens through this team.

Every large institution is its own environment, with its own core systems, telephony, CRM, compliance perimeter and operational reality. You work out what it takes for an AI system to hold up inside that specific environment, run the programme, and stay accountable until it is live and performing.

Our engagements run from focused proofs of concept to multi-year programmes inside India's biggest enterprises and government departments, worth crores and reaching millions of people. We are hiring across levels to cover that range.


ABOUT SARVAM

Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.



WHAT THIS ROLE PROMISES YOU

You own the outcome

You are not tracking someone else's plan. You own the scope, the timeline, and whether the numbers land. When a deployment works, it is because you made it work.

The room where AI meets the Indian economy

You will work directly with the leadership of India's largest banks, insurers and NBFCs, with central and state government departments, and with the fastest-moving companies in automotive, travel, healthcare, education and the digital-native economy. Different industries, different constraints, systems that go into live operation. Few roles in India offer this view of how AI actually reaches people.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own deployments end to end, from proof of concept through to the system running in production and hitting its committed KPIs.

 - Run the proof of concept where a customer needs to see it work before committing at scale. Getting to a convincing result quickly is often what unlocks the full deployment.

 - Do the implementation discovery a specific customer requires: their integrations, their processes, their data reality, their compliance constraints, their edge cases, and shape the solution around what you find.

 - Run the programme: plan, timelines, dependencies, risks, scope discipline, and the difficult conversations when something is off track.

 - Be the customer's point of contact through delivery.

 - Work with the deployment team on your engagement, whether that is Sarvam's Agent Engineers, certified partner teams, or both, and hold the delivery quality bar for the engagement.

 - Drive adoption on the ground. A system that works technically but is not used by the collections team, the branch staff or the citizen helpdesk has not landed. Getting it genuinely adopted is part of the job.

 - Own the documentation and operating charter for your deployment: how the system is run, monitored and scaled after go-live, so it holds up long after the launch.

 - Write the process and engagement playbooks that make the next deployment in that motion faster: how it gets scoped, planned, integrated and adopted.


WHO YOU ARE

We are hiring across levels, from 4+ years of experience. What matters more than years is whether you have owned an outcome in front of a customer and delivered it.

 - You have delivered, not just managed. You have owned client-facing delivery where the outcome was yours, whether that is a workstream inside a large programme or the whole programme itself. Most likely from consulting, high-quality systems integration, or an enterprise delivery organisation. You have carried a date and a number, not just a project plan.

 - You are technical enough to be taken seriously. You do not need to write production code, but you should be able to argue with an engineer about an integration approach, understand why an evaluation is failing, and reason about latency, reliability and scale without hand-waving.

 - You understand agentic AI. How LLMs and agents behave in production, why prompts and evaluations matter, and what breaks at scale. Ideally you have delivered AI systems yourself.

 - You have worked inside hard environments. Large regulated enterprises, banks, insurers, or the public sector, where procurement is slow, integration is messy, and change management is most of the job.

 - You communicate precisely. Crisp writing, clear escalation, no ambiguity about status.



Sarvam is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment regardless of background, identity, or personal characteristics. We believe the best AI for India can only be built by a team that reflects India.

title: Technical Partner Enablement Manager
description:
Sarvam Circle, our partner ecosystem, is one of our fastest growing vectors. It brings in firms to take frontier AI to government and public institutions, enterprises, and MSMEs across the country. title: Motion Designer
description:
ABOUT SARVAM

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Sarvam’s brand is already an argument about motion — it just hasn’t been allowed to move yet.

The monogram is a gateway that emerges — layered circles resolving out of mandala geometry into a single threshold form. The palette isn’t a set of swatches; it’s a continuous run from blue to orange, built to suggest progression and responsive state. Both of those ideas are about change over time. Both are currently being made mostly in stills.

We want the person who resolves that. Not someone to animate a logo once for a launch, but someone who decides how this brand behaves — how it enters, how it responds, how a gradient moves without becoming wallpaper — and then builds that language across films, web and product.

It’s a rare brief: a real identity with real motion logic baked into it, and nobody has run at it yet.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Define the motion language, not just the motion. Timing, easing, entrances, transitions, how the monogram behaves and how the gradient travels — documented and reusable, so the next fifty assets don’t start from zero.

 - Make the films. Model launches, product announcements, research drops, event opens, brand pieces. Concept, board, animate, edit, sound, deliver — you’ll own the shot end to end.

 - Make the product move too. Web animation, scroll behaviour, UI micro-interactions, demo and walkthrough videos. This is the half of the role that keeps the other half honest: motion that ships inside a live surface has constraints a film doesn’t.

 - Hand off cleanly to engineering. Lottie, Rive, sprite sequences, or a spec an engineer can actually build from. Work that dies in After Effects doesn’t count.

 - Solve the hard one: visualising speech. Our products are conversational — voice agents across 11 Indian languages, code-switching mid-sentence. Showing listening, thinking, speaking and switching, without falling back on a generic waveform, is the most interesting motion problem in the building.

 - Use AI properly in the pipeline. Generative video, boards and previz, roto, upscaling, variation. You should already be doing this, with a clear sense of where it saves a week and where it costs you the shot.

 - Work across the whole company. Design, marketing, product, research, founders. Rough briefs, hard launch dates, and work that still holds up at the end of it.
   
   


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years in motion design, in-house or at a studio, with a reel that shows both narrative work and work that shipped inside a product or website.

 - Deep After Effects. Shape layers, expressions, proper rigging — not template-and-swap. Plus real editing chops in Premiere or Resolve.

 - Figma is non-negotiable. Motion here starts inside the design system, not beside it.

 - Illustrator and Photoshop at working depth — you’ll be building and cleaning your own assets.

 - Fundamentals over flourish. Timing, weight, staging, anticipation, and how type behaves in motion. We will notice your easing curves.

 - Native fluency with AI tools in a professional motion workflow, and a point of view about it.

 - System thinking. Evidence you’ve taken a static identity and extended it into motion — or taken a motion system somewhere its guidelines hadn’t gone.

 - A real stake in this. You should care specifically about what Indian design deserves to look like in motion — and be a little impatient that it mostly doesn’t look like that yet.


BONUS POINTS

 - 3D — Blender or Cinema 4D, especially for abstract systems, geometry and product visualisation

 - Real-time or code-based motion: Rive, three.js, GLSL, TouchDesigner, Houdini

 - Sound design and mix — or at least strong instincts about audio driving picture

 - Indic typography in motion: animating Devanagari, Tamil or Kannada without breaking the letterforms

 


HOW TO APPLY

Send a reel — 90 seconds is plenty — plus a breakdown of what you did on each piece. Three shots you own completely beat a beautifully cut reel of team work. If one of them had to survive a real constraint — an engineer, a file size, a deadline, a language you don’t read — lead with that.

title: Software Engineer - Model API Platform
description:
About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC and LIC.


About the role

Sarvam's model APIs (ASR, TTS, Vision, LLM, Translate) are how developers and enterprises ship products on our foundation models. The platform handles tens of millions of API calls every day, over HTTP and WebSockets, with metering, billing, prepaid wallets and rate-limiting all part of the same stack.

We are hiring a Software Engineer to own major parts of this platform end to end, working closely with the Staff Engineer who leads its architecture. You will take an area such as speech to text pipeline,or text to speech pipeline, and be accountable for its reliability, performance and end-to-end latencies. This role is for someone who is obsessed with latencies, optimizes services and network paths to shave off milliseconds, ships fast, reasons from first principles, and treats AI as the default way to get engineering work done.


What you will do


Own a platform area end to end

• Own one or more major parts of the platform, such as the WebSocket streaming layer, a speech recognition pipeline, or text to speech pipeline: build, operate and improve them.

• Turn loosely defined goals into RFCs, milestones and shipped results, and write down the decisions and trade-offs.

• Be accountable after launch: on-call, incident response, root-cause analysis and follow-through on fixes.

• Make the call when a decision is needed, and own the outcome.

• Obsessed with latencies, dissecting existing services to understand the system, and tuning the right knobs to optimize performance.

• Bring services across without regressions in customer-facing APIs, latency or reliability.


Build real-time and model-serving pipelines

• Build and operate streaming infrastructure: WebSocket connections, long-lived sessions queue-based batch processing, backpressure and low-latency model invocation.

• Engineer audio pipelines: TTS chunking around model context limits, sample-rate conversion and format encoding, and VAD-based silence detection for ASR.

• Hold your services to sub-100ms latency SLOs in a multi-tenant environment, and know where every millisecond goes.


Think in systems and from first principles

• Reasons from constraints: latency budgets per hop, throughput, cost per request, failure modes and tenant isolation.

• Use back-of-the-envelope estimates to decide what to build, what to optimize and what to leave alone.

• Prefer simple designs you can fully explain over clever ones you cannot.

• Build in observability from day one: logging, metrics and tracing that let anyone debug production quickly.


Raise the bar for the team

• Strengthen the integration testing harness so the team can ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs.

• Partner with the Inference and MLOps teams on making model serving fast, reliable and operable.

• Mentor junior engineers through RFC reviews, code review and pairing.

• Practice design-first, documentation-first engineering: RFCs before code, no tribal knowledge.


What we are looking for

• 4–6 years of building and operating production backend systems.

• At least one service you owned end to end under real load, including what broke and what you changed.

• Strong distributed-systems fundamentals: concurrency, networking, queues, caching, consistency and failure modes.

• Experience with low-latency or high-throughput services, and comfort reasoning about p95 and p99 latency.

• Solid fundamentals with a relational database and a cache, such as PostgreSQL and Redis: schema design, query performance and caching strategy.

• Fluency in at least one backend language and willingness to work in both Python and Golang.

• Experience running services with containers, CI/CD and production monitoring.

• Daily, hands-on use of AI tools in your engineering workflow, with concrete examples of what you automated or sped up.

• A bias for action: fast on reversible decisions, careful on irreversible ones.

• Clear writing, especially RFCs and design docs that others can act on.


Good to have (not required)

• Voice AI or real-time audio experience: WebSockets, WebRTC, streaming ASR or TTS, or audio processing with FFmpeg or pyav, codecs, sample rates and VAD.

• Production experience in Go, or in Python with FastAPI.

• Experience serving LLM, ASR, TTS or vision models in production.

• Experience building metering, billing, wallet or payments infrastructure.

• Running services on Kubernetes in production.

• Time at an early- or growth-stage startup.


Why Sarvam

• A fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, with real population-scale impact.

• Researchers, engineers, builders and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar.

• High ownership and high impact from day one.

title: Software Development Engineer - Tejas
description:
Enterprises want agents that can do real work on their own data. That data sits across documents, databases and business systems that were never built for agents to read, and today's agents forget most of what they learn once a session ends.

Our team builds Sarvam's context engine to solve both problems. The knowledge side brings an enterprise's data together so agents can search it, navigate it and cite where an answer came from. The memory side lets agents remember what they learn over time, about individual users, about teams, and across the organisation. We want both to keep improving as they are used.

Knowledge and memory for agents is a rapidly evolving field. We want to build at the frontier of it, and to show with measurable results that our approach does better than traditional ones.



ABOUT SARVAM

Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.



WHAT THIS ROLE PROMISES YOU

You will join a small team and own large parts of the platform. The work is driven by real customer deployments, so what you build gets used quickly and you see what works and what does not. You will also work closely with the teams building Sarvam's models, document AI and inference, which makes it much easier to solve problems that cut across the stack.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and run the ingestion pipeline that parses, extracts and indexes large volumes of documents, and keep it reliable when files are messy and external services fail.

 - Connect to databases and enterprise systems so agents can work with structured records as well as documents.

 - Design how enterprise data is modelled, including the ontology, matching the same entity across sources, and tracing every value back to where it came from.

 - Build the retrieval tools agents call, with search, filters and citations, and make them fast and cheap enough for agents to use heavily.

 - Build memory for agents at the level of a user, a team and the whole organisation: how it is written, stored, retrieved and kept accurate over time.

 - Run evals, find where answers go wrong, and keep iterating until quality improves.

 - Work with product and forward-deployed engineers to turn what one customer needs into something the platform does for every customer.

 - Write design docs and keep decisions documented.

Our production stack is Go, with Temporal, OpenSearch and Postgres.



WHO YOU ARE

We are hiring at 3 to 5 years of experience.

 - You have built and run backend or data systems in production, and you have fixed them when they broke.

 - You are strong in at least one backend language. Our core is in Go, so Go experience is a plus, and you should be happy to work in it every day.

 - You have good fundamentals in data modelling and PostgreSQL.

 - You have worked on long-running pipelines and know how to make them safe to retry and recover.

 - You have worked on search or retrieval and know how to debug why the right result did not come back.

 - You use AI coding tools every day and have a good sense of where they help and where they don't.

 - You care about measuring quality, and you are comfortable building the evals to do it.


BONUS POINTS

 - Experience with knowledge graphs, ontologies, entity resolution or structured extraction.

 - Experience building memory for agents or LLM applications.

 - Document processing, such as OCR, layout or table extraction.

 - Connectors or change data capture for ERP, CRM or other enterprise systems.

 - Building on MCP, or serving LLMs and embedding models in production.

 - On-prem or air-gapped deployments.

 - Experience at an early- or growth-stage startup.

title: SDE3, Infrastructure Security Engineer (DevSecOps)
description:
About the team

Sarvam builds Indic-language AI used at population scale. The CPU Infrastructure team runs everything outside the GPU fleet: Kubernetes across Azure, AWS, GCP and Indian sovereign clouds, the network between them, Cloudflare, identity, secrets, observability, cost and the delivery pipeline every product ships through.

The team builds and runs what it builds. Engineers own real systems end to end, and every repeated piece of manual work is a candidate for automation. As an AI company, we are building AI agents into our own operations, to plan and review infrastructure changes, triage alerts and handle routine issues, with engineers setting the guardrails.

About the role

You are an infrastructure engineer whose first instinct is security, and who builds rather than only operates. You have worked on banking, fintech, payments or similarly regulated products, where a misconfiguration is an incident and an audit is routine. Here you set what “secure” means across Sarvam’s infrastructure and build the automation that enforces it, so security is a property of the pipeline rather than a review step. You work closely with the compliance team.

This is a hands-on role: most of your time goes into building, and you guide engineering teams across Sarvam on security — setting standards, reviewing security-relevant work and mentoring engineers.

Responsibilities

• Define and enforce security baselines for Kubernetes, cloud accounts, container images and CI/CD across all clouds

• Write the policy gates in the delivery pipeline (OPA / Conftest, Kyverno or equivalent): network exposure, IAM, image provenance, secrets, data residency

• Own secrets and workload identity: Vault or cloud-native equivalents, rotation, short-lived and scoped credentials, no long-lived keys

• Build detection and response: runtime security (Falco / Tetragon or equivalent), log-based detections, alerting and playbooks

• Run the finding-to-fix loop for security findings: triage, assign, fix, add a detection, retest

• Use LLMs and AI agents in security work: triaging findings, reviewing infrastructure changes, tuning detections, drafting incident timelines — and secure the agents themselves with scoped, short-lived permissions and audit trails

• Harden the supply chain: image signing and scanning, dependency policy, SBOMs

• Automate compliance evidence (CERT-In, ISO 27001, SOC 2, DPDP) together with the compliance team

• Set the security standards other engineers follow and review security-relevant changes

• Take part in on-call and lead security incidents

Requirements

• 5–9 years in DevOps, platform or security engineering, with at least 2 in a bank, fintech, payments company or other regulated environment

• Strong Kubernetes and Linux fundamentals; has run production clusters on at least one major cloud

• Hands-on with Terraform / OpenTofu and GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux)

• Has built security automation, not only operated tools: policy-as-code, secrets rotation, CI/CD security gates or detection pipelines

• Working knowledge of IAM, network security, TLS and secrets management across clouds

title: SDE2 - API Platform
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Sarvam's model APIs (LLM, ASR, TTS, Vision, Translate) are how developers and enterprises ship products on our foundation models. Our OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs route every request across multiple model deployments, with streaming, failover, metering, billing, and rate-limiting all part of the same stack. Today it's FastAPI and Python; we're in the middle of rewriting it in Go.

We're hiring a Software Engineer (SDE 2) to own core parts of this platform. The features. The reliability. The performance. This is an IC role.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Building and evolving the LLM API platform, from the moment a request hits the edge to the response that goes back out

 - The Python→Go rewrite: building services in Go alongside the existing Python stack, without compromising reliability

 - Streaming infrastructure: SSE for Chat Completions and Responses, long-lived connections, clean handling of cancellations and client disconnects

 - Routing and failover: weighted provider chains, retries with backoff, and latency-driven admission control across model deployments

 - Protocol compatibility: keeping the API faithful to the OpenAI spec across inference servers (vLLM, SGLang, Dynamo) that each behave slightly differently

 - The commercial layer: metering, billing, and rate-limiting, engineered to the same bar as the model APIs themselves

 - Performance and reliability for a multi-tenant platform serving long-context agentic and coding workloads

 - Observability (logging, metrics, tracing), so the team can debug production confidently and quickly

 - Integration and load testing: the harness that lets us ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs

 - Close partnership with the Inference and MLOps teams on production readiness for new model launches

 - Design-first, documentation-first engineering culture within the team: RFCs before code, decisions written down, no tribal knowledge



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years building production backend systems

 - Strong Python in production: asyncio, FastAPI or similar, and services you've built and operated under real load

 - Working knowledge of Go, or a strong willingness to learn it: you'll work in both languages through the rewrite

 - Experience building low-latency, multi-tenant backend services

 - Hands-on experience with streaming systems: SSE or WebSockets, long-lived connections, backpressure

 - Strong PostgreSQL and Redis fundamentals: schema design, query performance, caching, and rate limiting

 - Comfort running services on Kubernetes in production

 - An ownership mindset: you test before you ship, debug production with metrics, logs, and traces, and write the RCA afterwards



BONUS POINTS

 - Experience serving or integrating LLMs in production, especially OpenAI-compatible APIs

 - Familiarity with inference servers (vLLM, SGLang, Dynamo) and latency metrics such as time to first token and inter-token latency

 - Experience building metering, billing, or usage-based pricing infrastructure

 - Time at an early- or growth-stage startup: comfort with ambiguity, speed, and ownership

title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Infrastructure
description:
THE ROLE

Sarvam's products produce events, model traces, evals and billing data, and need to read that data back. The Data Platform team builds and runs the central data infrastructure every product uses: ingestion, streaming, the analytical warehouse, transformations, access control and audit.

We are hiring a Software Engineer / Senior Software Engineer (2–5 years of experience) to own this platform end to end. You will design, build and run systems that other teams depend on in production, and make real decisions on database internals, streaming and platform design. Stack: Go/Python, ClickHouse Cloud, Kafka, Avro, Airflow, dbt, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN & DO

 - Build and run the ingestion path: the service every product sends events to, Kafka behind it, and the pipes that land data in ClickHouse within seconds. Own schema validation, rate limits, dead-letter handling and the client SDKs.

 - Own the warehouse: ClickHouse Cloud. Design tables for the read path (sorting keys, partitions, materialized views, TTL), separate compute per workload, set per-user limits and per-tenant isolation, and attribute cost to the team that spent it.

 - Build reliable data pipelines and solve data problems: dbt models and Airflow DAGs with the BI engineers, CDC from product databases, sync and backfill jobs that are safe to re-run, and the data problems product teams bring you, such as a late source, a number that doesn't match or a query that has slowed down.

 - Make the platform self-serve: a registry of every dataset with its owner, schema, freshness and access; provisioning and permissions as code.

 - Run it in production: everything as Terraform and Helm with metrics, traces and alerts; be on call; handle incidents end to end, write the RCA and fix the root cause.

 - Grow the platform: new products keep arriving. You will help decide what the platform should do next and build it, whether that is a new source or sink, or a new way for teams to use the data.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 2–5 years of experience building, shipping and running large-scale, data-intensive systems in production, ideally at a startup where you owned things and were on call for them.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of: an OLAP database (ClickHouse preferred; Druid, BigQuery or Redshift also fine) or Kafka / event streaming. You understand how a columnar store writes, merges and scans data, or how a partitioned log gives ordering and delivery guarantees.

 - Experience with large-scale messaging systems like Kafka or RabbitMQ: partitions, consumer groups, delivery guarantees, backpressure.

 - Good at Go, or good at Python.

 - You know the usual data-system problems: schema evolution, idempotency, backpressure, partitioning, retention and TTL, CDC.

 - You have built or run at least one of: an event pipeline, a transformation layer (dbt, Spark or SQL on Airflow), a provisioning or control-plane service, or a multi-tenant data service with access control.

 - Comfortable with AWS, Kubernetes and Terraform in production.

 - You test before shipping, debug with metrics and traces, write RCAs, and document what you build.

 - Passion for data infrastructure and for enabling others by making their data easier to access.


NICE TO HAVE

 - ClickHouse in production: MergeTree, materialized views, projections, quotas, settings profiles, row policies, ClickHouse Cloud.

 - Kafka in depth: MSK, Kafka Connect, schema registry (Glue or Confluent), Avro.

 - dbt and Airflow at scale.

 - Audit or security data systems: append-only logs, integrity checks, tenant isolation.

 - OpenTelemetry, LLM observability (Langfuse or similar), eval pipelines.

 - Built an internal platform that other teams adopted.

title: SDE2 - Full Stack
description:
About the role

We're hiring two backend-heavy full-stack engineers (SDE 2 or SDE 3) for the Cowork team at Sarvam. Cowork is the agentic side of Indus: users hand it real work, and an agent plans, uses tools and connectors, works in a cloud sandbox, and hands back files, docs and artifacts across web, Android, iOS, macOS and Windows.

The role is full stack, but the centre of gravity is the backend: the BFF that every client talks to, and increasingly the agent harness behind it. You'll ship features end to end, from the API and data model through to the client screens on mobile, desktop and web.

What you'll work on

Most of your time goes into the BFF and the services around it; the rest into client work and the harness, depending on what the roadmap needs that quarter.

 - BFF (Chat Service): design and own the APIs that web, mobile and desktop share: sessions, conversations, streaming turns, artifacts, connectors, custom and managed agents. Data modelling, migrations, auth and RBAC, pagination and search.

 - Real-time streaming: stream LLM output, tool calls and agent events from the harness to clients over an event bus, and keep it correct under reconnects, retries and partial failures.

 - Agent harness and platform: contribute to Panja, our agent harness: tool and MCP integrations, sandboxed execution, file and artifact flows, latency and token-cost work.

 - Clients: build features end to end on our Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform apps (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows) and the Next.js web app, so a feature you design in the backend reaches users on every surface.

 - Production ownership: observability, on-call, RCAs, and making the system faster and cheaper with numbers to back it.


Tech stack

Python and PostgreSQL are the core; you don't need every item below on day one.

 - Backend: Python, SQLAlchemy + Alembic, PostgreSQL, OpenAPI

 - Supporting services: Go

 - Mobile and desktop: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows)

 - Web: Next.js, React, TypeScript


What we're looking for

A strong backend engineer who has also shipped real frontend work and is happy to keep doing both.

 - 3+ years (SDE 2) or 5+ years (SDE 3) building and running production backend services.

 - Deep in at least one backend language; Python preferred, Go, Kotlin/JVM or TypeScript/Node also welcome.

 - Solid API and data-model design: REST/streaming APIs, PostgreSQL schema design, migrations, indexing, transactions.

 - Distributed-systems fundamentals: async processing, queues or event streams, idempotency, retries, failure handling.

 - Production experience on Kubernetes or a similar platform, with observability you actually used to debug an incident.

 - Has shipped user-facing features on at least one client platform: Android, iOS, desktop or web (React/Next.js). Kotlin/Compose experience is a plus, not a gate.

 - Willing to pick up the side of the stack they know less, and to learn agent and LLM systems on the job.

 - Clear written communication: design docs, PR descriptions, RCAs.

Nice to have

 - Built on LLM APIs: tool calling, streaming, prompt caching, evals, or an agent loop of your own.

 - MCP servers or clients, OAuth connector integrations, or sandboxed code execution.

 - Kotlin Multiplatform / Compose Multiplatform, or native Android/iOS.

 - Real-time systems: WebSockets/SSE, NATS, Kafka, or Temporal-style durable workflows.

 - Go services, or performance and cost work with measurable before/after numbers.

 - Open-source work or public writing we can read.

title: AI Native Builder/Architect
description:
WHO WE ARE

Atlan is building the context layer for enterprise AI. Enterprises are pouring money into AI and most of it dies in production because the AI does not understand the business context around the data. That is the problem Atlan solves.

Gartner has named context the defining issue in enterprise AI, and calls context graphs the essential infrastructure for AI agents, naming Atlan one of three vendors already building it. We are also the only vendor named a Leader across all four major Gartner and Forrester evaluations for data catalogs, data governance and metadata management, the foundation the context layer runs on.

Come build the infrastructure that AI runs on.


WHO WE ARE

Gartner calls context the defining issue in enterprise AI, and context graphs the essential infrastructure for AI agents. It names Atlan as one of three vendors already building one. We're also the only vendor named a Leader in all four major Gartner and Forrester evaluations for data catalogs, data governance and metadata management, the layer our context graph is built on.

Come build the infrastructure AI runs on.



THE TEAM

You'll join the team building Atlan's context layer, the platforms that make it possible and the vertical agents that run on it. The platform is what any agent needs before an enterprise will trust it: a registry of which agents and skills exist, traces and evals on every run, and governance over cost and access.

Vertical agents each do one specific job, for customers and for Atlan's own teams. Inside Atlan they already run real work. There's an agent our CSMs trust, three GTM agents that replace 3,000 calls made by hand, an agent that watches every page on atlan.com http://atlan.com, and one that monitors the other agents. We write up what we learn in the open at Becoming Frontier https://atlan.com/frontier/.

The team works in small "two-slice" units. You own one initiative, usually with one or two people alongside you, and you decide how it gets built.



WHAT WILL YOU DO?

You'll take problems nobody has fully defined yet and ship working systems, fast. Depending on where you're matched, you may:

 - Own a 0→1 initiative from problem to production. Frame it, write the spec when there isn't one, pick the architecture and build it.

 - Build agents with the people who own the outcome, inside Atlan or at a customer. Scope the workflow with them, demo early and put the agent where the work already happens, like an approval in Slack or a redline in a legal team's Word doc.

 - Earn autonomy with evidence. Start with shadow runs, study the misses and widen what the agent can do as results support it.

 - Design for failure. Decide what happens when a tool is down, context is thin or the agent isn't sure, and how a person takes over.

 - Make the engineering calls on what stays deterministic code and what needs a model, build vs. reuse, model choice, cost and reliability. Explain the trade-offs clearly.

 - Make agent behavior observable. Tie traces and evals to the revision that ran. Track consistency, cost and latency alongside success rate, and treat drift as a regression.

 - Build on and extend the context layer, agent platform and registry: versioned skills, layered instructions, explicit permissions for tools and secrets, and model changes handled as migrations with evals rerun before promotion.

 - Build AI-native yourself. Run coding agents on your own work, keep their skills and instructions up to date, and review what they write for architectural drift.

 - Share what you learn. Turn what works into skills, reference architectures and quality gates that others adopt, and demo what you've built.


WHAT MAKES YOU A GREAT MATCH FOR US?


MUST HAVE

 - You've built software systems hands-on and shipped 0→1 products or platforms into production, often without a spec.

 - You've shipped agents or LLM systems that real people use. When one went wrong, you traced it back to the context, tool call or decision that caused it.

 - You use evals to find and fix real problems, check what a score actually counts, and judge agents by user impact: hours saved, error rate or cycle time.

 - You design for failure first: what the agent may touch, what happens when it's wrong, and where a person approves before it acts.

 - You build with coding agents every day and hold what they write to the same bar as your own code.

 - You're a critical optimist. You believe what agents can do is real, and test what still fails before trusting them with more.

 - You reason from first principles. When a familiar design doesn't fit, or a better model makes old scaffolding unnecessary, you notice and rebuild.

 - You have strong systems judgment. You can design for production reliability, latency, cost and security, build it yourself, and leave it in a shape others can build on.

 - You do your best work owning an initiative with one or two people alongside you, and don't need a large team to feel effective.


STRONG BONUS

 - Experience with MCP, A2A, agent frameworks and runtimes, LLM gateways or agent observability, or you've built an agent harness or orchestration layer yourself.

 - Experience with knowledge graphs, vector search, retrieval or semantic layers.

 - You've built an eval suite from scratch, or run shadow evaluations, LLM grading or staged rollouts.

 - You've shipped agents that write to a system of record, with permissions, approvals and an audit trail.

 - You've led AI adoption inside an engineering or business team and can show the before and after.

 - Founding-engineer, technical-founder or early-stage startup experience, where you built something from nothing.

 - A public trail of work, repos, demos, write-ups or talks, that shows how you build.

This role probably isn't for you if you want to manage a large team, want a well-scoped backlog handed to you, would rather build demos than run agents in production, or are still planning to get into AI.




WHY ATLAN?

Joining Atlan means being part of a global movement to help data teams do their life’s best work. Here’s what you can expect:

 - Competitive Compensation:  We benchmark at the top of the market and keep compensation simple: strong base salary, performance‑based variable pay, and impact‑driven equity (for most roles), so your total rewards grow in step with the value you create over time.

 - AI Native Culture: Atlan is where AI-native builders come to build the systems the future of work will run on. AI isn’t an add-on, it’s woven into how we build, think, and work every day, empowering every Atlanian to move faster and create a bigger impact.

 - Health & Wellness: From Day‑1 health, dental, vision, and mental health to flexible health stipends, we design benefits offerings that lead in each country we're in.

 - Flexible Time Off & Leave Policies: We trust you to own your energy: flexible time off and modern leave so you can unplug properly, support yourself and your loved ones, and come back ready to drive an impact.

 - Accelerated Growth & Learning: Develop at an uncommon velocity through cutting-edge tech, complex implementations, and an experienced team that values mastery.

 - Global, Remote-First, High-Trust:  Work from anywhere with a diverse team across 15+ countries, in a trust-first, async environment that gives you true flexibility and ownership over how you work.



More About Us

Atlan is building the shared context layer that enterprises need so AI can operate on trusted, governed context. The conversation has moved from data leaders asking:  “Can we trust the data in our stack?” to businesses asking: “Can we trust AI inside the business?”

We are the missing infrastructure for businesses becoming AI-forward - the connective tissue between their data stack, operational systems, and AI agents.

To learn more, visit www.atlan.com http://www.atlan.com and follow us on LinkedIn. https://www.linkedin.com/company/atlan-hq/posts/?feedView=all


Equal Opportunity Employer

Atlan is committed to building an inclusive, diverse, and authentic workplace. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.



Recruitment Fraud Alert
Your safety is important to us. Be cautious of recruiting emails from domains other than @atlan.com http://atlan.com. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links — visit atlan.com/careers http://atlan.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

Atlan will never ask candidates to make a payment to apply for or obtain a position. We also will never request financial information, passwords, or other sensitive information from candidates. If you receive a communication that you believe may not be legitimate, do not send money or sensitive information. Please report the same on privacy@atlan.com.

title: Senior Consulting Engineer - India
description:
ClickHouse is the open-source, real-time analytical database behind a lot of today's AI. More than 4,000 companies build on ClickHouse, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Tesla and Meta.

As a Consulting Engineer, you're the hands-on engineer on our customers' most important projects. When a customer needs to migrate, integrate, or prove ClickHouse on a real workload, you work in the build alongside their engineers: you design it, build it, test it and hand it over.

You'll work on a broad mix of projects for customers across India, from moving large workloads off other databases to building new real-time analytics on ClickHouse. Each one is scoped with clear goals from the start, so you know what success looks like and can get stuck in. It's a fast way to build deep experience across lots of different data problems.

The consulting function at ClickHouse is less than a year old, so you'll help shape how ClickHouse delivers this work as the team grows. Between projects you take cases alongside support engineers, which keeps you close to day-to-day support.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Turn customer goals into a scoped project with measurable success criteria, sizing and a timeline

 - Design a target architecture and prove it against the customer's own data: schema and engine design, capacity and sizing, proofs of concept

 - Do the build: implementation, pipelines and integrations, migration execution, tooling and automation

 - Measure it before it matters, with benchmarking, load and functional testing, then support the cutover

 - Tune what production reveals, then hand over with an engagement report and knowledge transfer, so the customer's team can run it without you

 - Take L1 to L3 cases alongside support engineers when you're between projects

 - Feed what you see in the field back to Product and Engineering, and turn your work into reference architectures, knowledge base articles and blog posts

 - Work in a constant feedback loop with the Pre-sales team to ensure that the demos and POCs they present are credible when you put them into production

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 5+ years delivering hands-on technical work for customers, whether your title was consultant, professional services, solutions architect, senior support, SRE or something else

 - Real depth in databases, whether analytical, transactional or relational

 - Hands-on SQL. You regularly write complex queries from scratch, and tune and debug them yourself

 - You've owned implementations, migrations or POCs for external customers from start to finish

 - Hands-on cloud experience (AWS, GCP and/or Azure)

 - You've deployed and run workloads on Kubernetes yourself

 - You've run distributed systems, such as distributed databases, in production

 - You give precise technical answers and explain them clearly

 - Fluent English

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with ClickHouse

 - Migrating analytical workloads from systems such as PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery or Elastic

 - Terraform

 - Data pipelines and streaming, such as Kafka, Kinesis, Spark or Debezium

 - Python, Bash or Go

 - Involvement in open source, as a user, contributor or community member

GOOD TO KNOW

 - This role is remote in India

 - Travel to customer sites is part of the job, up to 35% of your time, depending on the project: some need none, others weekly visits

 - You'll join our India Support Services team, alongside Support Engineers and TAM Architects

 - You'll be part of the on-call rotation, about one week a quarter, with time off in lieu if you're paged at a weekend

HOW WE HIRE

 - A 30-minute call with our recruiter

 - A conversation with the hiring manager

 - A take-home exercise, designed to take three to four hours, with three working days to complete it

 - A 90-minute technical interview with the team: you'll walk us through your take-home, then join a working session where you write and tune SQL live

 - A final conversation with our VP of Support Services

 - References, then an offer

The working session is without AI tools, so make sure you're comfortable writing queries from scratch. Download open-source ClickHouse and practise: it's free, easy to install, and great preparation.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Identity & Authorization Platform
description:
The Platform Auth team’s goal is to support our ‘one customer identity’ vision by providing tools, processes, and expertise for our engineering teams to create a unified access management experience while simplifying and standardizing engineering patterns in the space. We are looking for engineers to join our growing team! 

What you will be doing:

 - Design and build the platform services that power authentication, authorization, and audit across ClickHouse Cloud. This includes a unified RBAC/ReBAC service, token issuance and session handling, and the SDKs that product teams embed to make authorization decision.

 - Model permissions and access control primitives (resources, roles, relationships, policies) that work across ClickHouse, SQL Console, ClickPipes, and HyperDX. Ship the libraries and APIs that other engineers build against.

 - Implement protocol-level support for SAML, SCIM, OIDC, OAuth2, and MFA/passwordless flows. Own the integrations that make enterprise SSO and provisioning work end to end.

 - Build the audit and authorization-decision telemetry pipeline so every access decision is observable, queryable, and surfaceable to customers.

 - Partner with product engineering teams to migrate bespoke per-product auth implementations onto the shared platform, and design APIs that make adoption straightforward.

 - Carry the platform on-call rotation and own production reliability for systems on the critical path of every customer request.

What you bring along:

 - Minimum 4+ years building production backend systems at scale. Comfort with at least one systems language (Go, Rust, C++) and one application language (TypeScript, Python).

 - Hands-on experience designing and implementing an authentication or authorization service. Examples include building a token issuer, an OIDC or OAuth2 provider, a policy engine, a permissions model, or an FGA/ReBAC system in the style of Zanzibar, OpenFGA, SpiceDB, or Cedar.

 - Working knowledge of SAML, SCIM, OIDC, and OAuth2 at the protocol level and are able to implement them.

 - Experience designing APIs and SDKs that other engineers depend on, with strong opinions on what makes them adoptable.

 - Experience operating distributed systems at scale, including caching strategies, consistency tradeoffs, and multi-region concerns.

 - Familiarity with identity vendors (Auth0, WorkOS, AWS/GCP/Azure IAM) as building blocks you've extended or integrated into a larger platform.

 - Strong production debugging instincts and a high bar for systems that are easy to develop against.

Bonus:

 - You've built or contributed to a Zanzibar-style authorization system, or run an OpenFGA or SpiceDB deployment beyond the demo.

 - You've designed a multi-tenant permission model that survived real customer requirements like custom roles, hierarchies, delegation, and ABAC attributes.

 - You've shipped an SDK that product teams across an org actually adopted, and have opinions about why most internal SDKs fail.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Notion is looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer focused on migrations to join our growing team in India. You will help deliver complex, production-grade data migrations, integrations, and automations for customers across APAC.

This is initially an internally focused, hands-on engineering role. You will partner closely with regional Forward Deployed Engineers, who own customer discovery, solution architecture, stakeholder communication, risk management, and final customer validation. You will own the behind-the-scenes technical execution layer from feasibility assessment and implementation through testing, production rollout, QA, reconciliation, reporting, and operational handoff.

You will work across multiple customer environments and source systems, often with incomplete requirements, imperfect data, and real-world constraints. Success requires strong engineering fundamentals, sound judgment, careful validation, and the ability to turn one-off delivery work into reusable tools and repeatable playbooks.

As a founding engineer in India, you will help build a new regional engineering capability from the ground up. You will create migration infrastructure, standards, and reusable tooling used by FDEs across APAC, while establishing practices that can scale globally. The role offers an opportunity to become a technical authority for production migration delivery, shaping how Notion approaches reliability, validation, and operational quality across complex customer environments. As the team grows, the role may also expand toward customer-facing FDE work, technical leadership, or a deeper engineering path, depending on business needs and demonstrated capability.




WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE:

 - Own the technical execution layer after customer requirements, scope, and solution architecture have been established with the regional FDE. Contribute to feasibility assessment, estimation, implementation planning, and risk identification while the regional FDE remains accountable for customer discovery, scope, architecture, stakeholder communication, and final acceptance.

 - Apply a repeatable migration lifecycle covering source inventory and sampling, scope and pruning decisions, compatibility and degradation assessment, transformation design, pilot or dry run, user acceptance testing, production cutover, reconciliation, remediation, hypercare, and documented handoff.

 - Translate approved customer and regional FDE requirements into clear technical designs, implementation plans, test strategies, runbooks, and delivery estimates.

 - Build production-quality migration utilities, backend services, data pipelines, integrations, and automations using Python, SQL, APIs, databases, and cloud infrastructure.

 - Investigate source-system behavior, data quality issues, permissions, rate limits, authentication constraints, and edge cases, then recommend practical solutions.

 - Design and validate permissions, ownership, and inheritance mappings against the approved migration plan. Make unsupported or ambiguous access requirements explicit, obtain the required decision or approval, and preserve evidence of validation.

 - Design migrations for reliability, scale, security, observability, idempotency, failure recovery, and safe reruns.

 - Execute migrations only through approved environments, devices, accounts, and tooling. Follow least-privilege access, customer-specific security and data-residency requirements, and approved handling procedures. Do not store customer data in unmanaged local or external systems, and escalate privacy, security, or sovereignty concerns before execution.

 - Build validation and reconciliation frameworks that provide clear evidence of migration completeness, accuracy, and exceptions.

 - Debug failures across application code, infrastructure, customer data, third-party systems, and the Notion platform, then drive issues through resolution.

 - Manage multiple implementation workstreams, dependencies, and priorities while communicating scope, progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly.

 - Surface scope changes, unsupported requirements, timeline risks, and material effort increases early. Document assumptions and trade-offs, and escalate with options and a recommended path rather than silently absorbing additional work.

description:
About the Team

Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.

About the Role

As an Incident Commander on Detection & Response, you’ll lead the response to complex security incidents affecting OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and infrastructure. You’ll establish response priorities, coordinate technical work streams, drive containment and recovery decisions within agreed authority, and keep stakeholders informed as facts evolve. You’ll work with security and infrastructure teams across endpoints, identity, cloud, and compute environments, maintaining clear ownership and effective handoffs across time zones. Detection engineering knowledge is a supporting requirement: you’ll use telemetry and detection logic to assess evidence, identify visibility gaps, and guide improvements that make incident response more effective.

In this role, you will:

 - Run incident command from initial assessment through containment, recovery, and closure, establishing severity, scope, response objectives, and escalation needs.

 - Assign work stream owners and coordinate investigation, containment, and recovery in parallel. Maintain a decision log and distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions.

 - Drive timely containment and recovery decisions with the appropriate owners, weighing security risk, evidence preservation, and operational impact within agreed decision rights.

 - Communicate incident status, impact, uncertainty, actions underway, and the next update to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

 - Manage cross-time-zone handoffs with explicit command ownership, current status, outstanding risks, pending decisions, and next actions.

 - Improve response readiness through exercises, playbooks, and post-incident reviews; track agreed corrective actions with their owners.

 - Partner with detection engineers to evaluate telemetry and detection quality, close incident-related visibility gaps, and prioritize practical response automation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have personally led complex security incidents as incident commander or an equivalent response lead, with clear examples of decisions, delegation, escalation, and outcomes.

 - Make sound decisions with incomplete information and revise them as evidence changes, balancing containment urgency with operational impact.

 - Coordinate responders across teams and time zones, resolve conflicting priorities, and maintain clear ownership during handoffs.

 - Communicate calmly and precisely under pressure, including concise stakeholder updates and explicit statements of uncertainty.

 - Have the security and infrastructure fundamentals to challenge investigation findings and assess containment and recovery options.

 - Understand detection engineering, including telemetry coverage, detection logic, false positives and false negatives, and validation. Can query and interpret evidence to support response decisions.

 - Turn incident lessons into practical improvements to readiness, playbooks, detection coverage, and response tooling.

title: Head of India Policy, Global Affairs
description:
About the Team:
OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence (AGI) benefits all of humanity. Achieving this goal requires more than cutting-edge research—it demands deep, ongoing engagement with the policymakers, communities, and institutions shaping the future of AI.

The Global Affairs team leads this engagement. We cultivate authentic, collaborative relationships with public officials, regulators, multilateral bodies, civil society leaders, and the broader AI policymaking community to ensure that diverse perspectives inform our work. By bringing external insights into OpenAI and sharing our own learnings transparently, we help advance thoughtful regulation, responsible industry standards, and governance frameworks that promote the safe and beneficial development of AI technologies.

In close partnership with our research, product, and policy colleagues, we work across regions to anticipate emerging issues, craft forward-looking strategies, and champion policies that align technological progress with human values. Our mission is to help shape the global conversation on AI and ensure that the benefits of this transformative technology reach people everywhere.

 

About the Role

As Head of India Policy, Global Affairs you will lead OpenAI’s public policy strategy, government engagement, and policy partnerships in India. You will help shape an environment that supports safe AI development and deployment, expands access to its benefits, and advances India’s ambitions for innovation and economic opportunity.

You will serve as a senior policy representative to Indian institutions and build partnerships that turn shared priorities into practical results. Working with Global Affairs leaders worldwide and colleagues in India, you will connect national and state priorities with OpenAI’s work on responsible adoption, public services, AI skills, and research.

This role is based in New Delhi, India, and requires travel within India and internationally.

In this role, you will

 - Set and execute OpenAI’s India policy strategy, translating global priorities into focused national campaigns with clear goals, milestones, and measures of policy progress and public benefit.

 - Build durable relationships with central and state governments, Parliament, regulators, industry, and civil society. Engage constructively across political perspectives and bring local insights into OpenAI’s decisions.

 - Develop policy positions, consultation responses, and advocacy on AI governance, safety, privacy, copyright, and liability, working closely with Legal and specialist policy teams.

 - Anticipate political and regulatory developments and give leadership clear, actionable advice on risks, opportunities, and tradeoffs affecting OpenAI and the people who use our products.

 - Design and deliver partnerships with government, universities, nonprofits, and industry that strengthen AI fluency, support research, and improve public services. Advance local-language access and measure sustained use and outcomes for underserved communities.

 - Work with commercial, technical, and infrastructure colleagues to address policy and procurement barriers to responsible adoption and support AI infrastructure opportunities aligned with India’s needs.

 - Coordinate policy engagement around product launches and sensitive issues, including youth safety, election integrity, and cybersecurity. Partner with central response teams to ensure timely, accurate engagement with public institutions.

 - Represent OpenAI in policy forums and support senior executive engagements. Lead cross-functional projects and external advisers with disciplined prioritization, resource management, and follow-through.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

 - 10 or more years of relevant experience in public policy, government, technology, or international affairs, including responsibility for senior stakeholder engagement in India.

 - Understand India’s political institutions, central and state policymaking, and digital economy, and have a record of building trust with senior public officials and diverse communities.

 - Have delivered meaningful policy outcomes and complex partnerships, with evidence of your ability to set strategy, build coalitions, and carry work through implementation.

 - Understand AI policy and can quickly develop fluency in technical issues, explain them clearly, and exercise sound judgment about innovation, safety, and public trust.

 - Lead through influence across legal, research, product, communications, and commercial teams, and turn competing priorities into clear decisions and coordinated action.

title: Senior HR Business Partner, India
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The HR Business Partner team at OpenAI supports managers and employees as teams grow, perform and adapt. We work alongside managers at all levels to resolve day-to-day people challenges, build management capability and create the conditions for teams to do their best work.

Our expertise spans team effectiveness, talent development, manager coaching, employee relations and change management, grounded in our Contributions & Impact (C&I) culture. We operate with urgency, empathy and sound judgment, valuing sincerity, collaboration and meaningful impact.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Senior HR Business Partner. This role will primarily support teams in India, with a focus on Go-to-Market and selected other functions. The portfolio may also include support for teams in other APAC markets as business needs evolve. You’ll provide hands-on support to managers at all levels, owning day-to-day people work and helping teams grow and scale effectively.

Your GTM partnership will span teams such as Sales, Technical Success, Partnerships and Marketing. Across your portfolio, you’ll build a deep understanding of business priorities and use that context to prioritise and deliver practical people support.

As a hands-on partner to managers at all levels, you will use independent judgment to coach managers, resolve people issues and follow through on day-to-day work as teams scale. You will own delivery across your portfolio, working closely with the International HRBP Leader, Recruiting, Finance, Employment Legal and People centres of expertise, and involving specialist partners when needed.

This is an individual contributor role, based in Mumbai or Bangalore. We operate in a hybrid work model: three days in the office per week. 

 


YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own day-to-day people support across your portfolio, with a primary focus on GTM. Be a practical point of contact for managers on performance, employee relations, team changes and development. Prioritise issues, agree clear next steps and see them through to resolution as teams scale.

 - Support teams as they grow. Help managers put agreed team structures and workforce plans into practice, clarify roles and address capacity needs as teams across your portfolio grow and scale existing operations. Coordinate with Finance and Recruiting to support hiring and team changes.

 - Build manager effectiveness. Coach managers at all levels, from first-time managers to experienced people managers, on feedback, difficult conversations, team dynamics and accountability. Help them address everyday people challenges with clarity and care.

 - Build capability and succession. Help managers identify skills and development needs across GTM teams. Partner on talent reviews, succession planning, internal mobility and development, with particular attention to roles essential to customer and business outcomes.

 - Drive performance and rewards decisions. Help managers set clear expectations, address underperformance and recognise contributions consistently. Partner with Compensation and Sales Compensation specialists on people implications of incentive structures, role changes and rewards decisions.

 - Lead through organisational change. Guide organisational changes and sensitive employee matters across your portfolio, partnering with Employment Legal and Employee Relations specialists. Balance business urgency, local requirements and fair, consistent treatment.

 - Use insight to act early. Combine workforce data, business context and employee feedback to identify emerging risks, test assumptions and recommend action. Track whether interventions improve capability, retention and team effectiveness.

 - Scale effective People practices. Partner with global HRBPs and centres of expertise to evolve performance, engagement and talent programmes across your portfolio, ensuring local needs inform global decisions and local delivery remains practical.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Substantial HRBP experience. Typically 7–10+ years in HR, including at least five years supporting managers and teams in high-growth, international or complex organisations. We value the scope and impact of your experience.

 - Commercial understanding. Experience supporting Sales and other go-to-market functions, with an understanding of enterprise sales cycles, customer-facing roles and the people implications of commercial operating models.

 - Hands-on manager partnership. A record of supporting managers at all levels, resolving day-to-day people issues and owning delivery across a busy portfolio. You can exercise independent judgment, challenge constructively and build trusted relationships.

 - India experience. Experience supporting teams in India, navigating local business and employment environments, with sound judgment about when to involve specialist partners.

 - Organisational and talent judgment. Practical experience supporting team growth, workforce planning, manager coaching, performance management and talent development, including delivering change through ambiguity.

 - Analytical and execution strength. The ability to diagnose problems using data and context, make clear recommendations and follow through. You prioritise effectively, take ownership of complex people issues and stay close to the details through resolution.

We're Redis. We built the product that runs the fast apps our world runs on. (If you checked the weather, used your credit card, or looked at your flight status online today, you’re welcome.) At Redis, you’ll work with the fastest, simplest technology in the business—whether you’re building it, telling its story, or selling it to our 10,000+ worldwide customers. We’re creating a faster world with simpler experiences. You in?


ABOUT THE COMPANY

We are a growing software company building products that help customers work more efficiently and make better decisions. As we scale, we are investing in the systems, processes, and people that support a reliable, well-controlled finance function.
 This is an opportunity to join a lean, collaborative team where your work will have visible impact. You will help turn business requirements into scalable finance workflows and practical system improvements.






THE TEAM

Why will you enjoy this new opportunity?



You will own the day-to-day administration and continuous improvement of the finance systems that keep the business running. This role combines hands-on NetSuite ownership, cross-functional problem solving, and process design. You will work closely with Accounting, FP&A, Procurement, People, IT, and business leaders, with the autonomy to improve how work gets done and the visibility to see the impact of those improvements.






THE ROLE

●   Serve as the primary administrator and internal subject matter expert for NetSuite, managing roles, permissions, workflows, forms, saved searches, reports, dashboards, custom fields, and custom records.

●   Configure and administer NetSuite capabilities, including Financials, Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay, Fixed Assets, Advanced Revenue Recognition, MCP, SuiteAnalytics, dashboards, saved searches, workflows, roles, permissions, and user access.

●   Support reporting, dashboards, saved searches, and ad hoc analysis so finance and business partners can make informed decisions.

●   Evaluate and support related finance and procurement tools, including Zip






WHAT YOU'LL BRING

●   7+ years of hands-on experience in NetSuite administration in a business environment (required).

●   Experience successfully supporting or leading one to two full-lifecycle NetSuite implementations, from requirements and design through configuration, data migration, testing, deployment, and post-go-live support.

●   Strong understanding of ERP concepts, financial systems, and core Finance processes, including the general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, order management, procurement, revenue recognition, and financial reporting.

●   Ability to operate as a hands-on individual contributor while serving as the internal go-to resource for NetSuite knowledge and support; highly organized, detail-oriented, and accountable for data quality and system reliability.
