title: Staff Software Engineer - Frontend
description:
We’re looking for frontend engineers who are excited about:

 - Building data-intensive products that developers use for hours every day

 - Making complex, multi-module workflows feel simple and intuitive

 - Pushing React performance so the UI never gets in the way—especially during a production incident




ABOUT SIGNOZ

SigNoz is an open-source observability platform that brings metrics, logs, and traces into one product.

Our frontend is built with React and TypeScript and helps engineering teams explore large volumes of telemetry data, investigate problems, and resolve incidents faster.



Today, SigNoz has:

 - 31,500+ GitHub stars

 - 8,000+ members in our Slack community

 - 900+ customers

 - Users processing petabytes of telemetry data across the world




WHAT YOU’LL DO

This role goes beyond implementing screens from specifications. You’ll own meaningful parts of the product experience from problem definition to production.



You will:

 - Design and build complex workflows across dashboards, traces, logs, metrics, alerts, and infrastructure monitoring

 - Own large frontend features and systems end-to-end

 - Turn technically complex observability concepts into clear, intuitive experiences

 - Architect for performance using techniques such as virtualization, progressive loading, smart caching, and selective rendering

 - Profile and improve slow interactions, large visualizations, and data-heavy views

 - Contribute to our frontend architecture, design system, and engineering standards

 - Work closely with design, product, founders, and backend engineers

 - Speak with users and ship improvements that help engineers investigate incidents faster

 - Help other engineers make better frontend and product decisions






WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

You may be a good fit if:

 - You have strong experience building production applications with React and TypeScript

 - You think in systems and user journeys—not just individual screens

 - You care about product experience as much as code quality

 - You have worked on complex, data-heavy, or highly interactive applications

 - You understand React rendering behaviour and know how to find performance bottlenecks

 - You are comfortable using browser profiling and debugging tools

 - You can make thoughtful trade-offs between performance, maintainability, and delivery speed

 - You take ownership and can move work forward without detailed instructions

 - You communicate clearly and work well across engineering, design, and product

Experience with observability is helpful, but not required. Curiosity and the ability to understand complex technical domains matter more.






PROBLEMS YOU MIGHT WORK ON

 - Rendering dashboards containing many charts and large datasets without slowing down the browser

 - Building fast and intuitive experiences for exploring millions of logs or traces

 - Visualizing complex distributed traces and service relationships

 - Creating consistent interactions across multiple product modules

 - Improving loading, filtering, navigation, and debugging workflows during live incidents

 - Evolving a large frontend codebase while the product and team continue to grow






HOW WE WORK

 - We are remote-first and have no offices. Work from wherever you do your best work.

 - We are a small, experienced team, so individual contributions have visible impact.

 - Engineers have meaningful ownership over both technical decisions and the product experience.

 - We move quickly, talk directly with users, and continuously improve what we ship.



Observability is a large and growing market, but more importantly, it is a space full of difficult product and engineering problems.



If you enjoy React and TypeScript, care deeply about UX and performance, and want to build tools that engineers rely on every day, we’d love to hear from you.

title: AI GTM Engineer
description:
AI GTM ENGINEER




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an AI GTM Engineer  to own the systems, data, and processes behind our marketing engine.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll work across Marketing, Sales, Product and Growth to make sure our campaigns run smoothly, our data is reliable, and we’re continuously improving conversion across the funnel.

You should be equally comfortable building a dashboard, fixing an email workflow, creating an account list, and figuring out why a conversion rate dropped.

What you'll build

 - Signal queues for sales. Define and ship signals such as ICP signups, usage spikes, expansion and win-back triggers, delivered to reps as ranked queues in HubSpot and Slack.

 - Data Pipelines: Build and maintain data pipelines for ingesting intent signals from various sources

 - Customer health and alerting. Build usage and billing-spike alerts so CS and Sales act on changes in paying accounts.

 - A trusted funnel. Build one source of truth for signup to SQL to closed-won in BigQuery, trusted by every GTM lead.

 - AI-native GTM workflows. Use LLMs and agents for enrichment, research, scoring and personalization, and measure how accurate they are. 

 - CRM automation. Automate lead routing, lifecycle stages and data hygiene end to end, with zero manual lead assignment.

 - Build a self improving GTM system using LLMs and connectors to data source. Incorporate feedback mechanism so that the system improves over time
   

You'll also own

 - GTM tooling across HubSpot, Customer.io http://Customer.io, Clay, Lemlist and n8n

 - Email journeys for prospects, product users and customers, including segmentation and experiments

 - Account lists, enrichment and measurement for ABM and outbound campaigns



Who would be a good fit

 - Experience in building data pipelines to get signals from different sources

 - Strong SQL. You're comfortable in BigQuery or a similar warehouse and build pipelines yourself.

 - You have 3+ yrs of experience either on engineering or GTM side or mix of two

 - You can work with APIs, especially CRM APIs like HubSpot's.

 - You define signals, not just implement them: you have a view on what makes an account worth calling, and you check that view against what actually closes.

 - You've worked closely with sales or growth teams, or you're eager to sit with reps and learn what they need.

 - Interest in understanding how GTM works and ideating ways to find new intent signals

 - You ship scrappily on your own, without needing a data team around you.

 - You can work async with some overlap with US hours.

Bonus points

 - Experience at a PLG, developer tools, infrastructure or open-source company

 - Hands-on experience with HubSpot, Clay, Customer.io http://Customer.io or n8n

 - You've built entity resolution or enrichment pipelines (for example, domain or IP to company)

 - You've shipped LLM or agent workflows in production and measured their accuracy

 - You've used product usage data to drive sales or expansion

title: Demand Gen Lead
description:
WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

SigNoz is an open source observability platform built on OpenTelemetry: logs, metrics and traces in one tool. It's designed for an era where agents and humans run observability together. We are a YC company with 32K+ GitHub stars, and revenue grew 4x in 2025.


We have more buying signal than most companies our size. Thousands of teams run SigNoz self-hosted, hundreds of teams sign up for SigNoz Cloud every month, and we have product usage data for all of them. Very little of that signal gets acted on today. Your job is to turn it into pipeline.


You will work directly with the founders. We are looking for a builder: someone who sets up systems that keep working and scale well as we grow, not someone who runs one campaign after another by hand.




WHAT YOU WILL OWN




1. SIGNAL-BASED OUTBOUND (THE BIGGEST LEVER)

 - Decide which signals mean an account is worth reaching out to: ICP signups, usage spikes, trial activity, large self-hosted installs, teams hiring for observability or platform roles, and companies moving off an incumbent tool.

 - Turn each signal into a play. Decide who to contact, what to say, which channel (email, LinkedIn), what runs automated and what gets a personal touch, and when an account goes to an AE.

 - Write and run the sequences yourself at first. Track reply, meeting and pipeline rates for each play, and kill the plays that don't convert.

 - Work with our GTM Engineer, who builds the data and signal queues. You decide which signals matter and what we do with them. They make the signals reliable and automated.

 - Own the handoff to sales: what counts as a qualified meeting, response SLAs, and a weekly loop on lead quality.
   
   


2. LIFECYCLE EMAIL

 - Own the email journeys at every stage:
   
   - New signups, from onboarding through activation
   
   - Trials, through conversion to paid
   
   - Paying customers, toward expansion and annual plans
   
   - Self-hosted open source users, toward SigNoz Cloud or Enterprise

 - Build campaigns triggered by product usage: first data sent, usage milestones, trial expiry, usage drops and billing changes.

 - Write the way engineers like to be written to: plain, specific and useful. Run A/B tests, watch deliverability, and report what each journey adds to activation and revenue.
   


3. SOCIAL AND PAID (A PLUS, NOT CORE)

These aren't core skills for this role. If you understand them, that's a bonus, and you'll get to use them:

 - Run SigNoz on LinkedIn and X in formats native to each platform. Help the founders and DevRel get their best material in front of the right people.

 - Run paid experiments through an agency or freelancers first: Google on brand and competitor terms, and LinkedIn and Reddit retargeting. Scale only what pays back.


ACROSS ALL OF IT

 - Agree pipeline targets with the founders, then own the number.

 - Build funnel reporting with the GTM Engineer so everyone knows what converts and what doesn't.

 - Work with Product Marketing and DevRel on messaging. Join the weekly pipeline review with sales.
   


HOW THE ROLE GROWS

This role starts hands-on. For the first few quarters you will run the programs yourself: writing sequences, building journeys and launching campaigns. We are not looking for someone who needs a team before anything happens.

Once your programs reliably produce pipeline, you build the team. The first hires will likely cover lifecycle, outbound/SDR, and social and content.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - 30 days: You know the product, the users and the data. You've audited our current email journeys and signals, and your first signal-based outbound play is live.

 - 90 days: Three or more outbound plays are running with measured meeting rates. Onboarding and trial journeys have been rebuilt, and nurture for open source users is live. The funnel baseline is agreed and trusted.

 - 12 months: Demand gen is a predictable, measured source of qualified pipeline. Signup-to-SQL conversion is clearly up, and you've made your first hires.


WHO WE THINK FITS

 - 6+ years in demand gen, growth or lifecycle marketing at B2B software companies, selling to technical buyers in the US.

 - You've run outbound built on data and intent signals, not on bought lists. You can walk us through plays you designed and the meetings and pipeline they produced.

 - You've owned lifecycle email end to end on a self-serve or PLG product: segmentation, triggers, copy, testing and deliverability.

 - You write well, and engineers don't tune out when they read it.

 - You're comfortable with the math: attribution, conversion rates, CAC payback, and pipeline by channel.

 - You're a builder. You set up systems, automation and processes that keep running without you and scale as volume grows.

 - You measure yourself by pipeline and revenue, not MQLs.

 - You've worked hands-on with modern GTM tools (HubSpot, Customer.io http://Customer.io, Clay, Lemlist or similar) and have opinions on where AI actually helps.

 - You can overlap with US mornings (India evenings) a few times a week.


BONUS POINTS

 - A background in engineering, and you can understand technical terms

 - You've managed or mentored a small team

 - You've run paid campaigns on LinkedIn, Google or Reddit, directly or through an agency

 - You've grown a dev-facing social account


WHY SIGNOZ

 - Real product pull. This isn't cold-start demand. Thousands of teams already use SigNoz.

 - Work directly with the founders, with a budget and a clear path to running the function.

 - A global dev-infra product, backed by YC and leading Bay Area VCs. Fully remote.

title: Sr Product Manager - IC
description:
ABOUT SIGNOZ

SigNoz is an open-source observability platform that helps modern engineering teams monitor, debug, and optimize their applications with deep visibility into metrics, traces, and logs — all in one place. We’re built natively on OpenTelemetry and offer both self-hosted and cloud options, so teams can run observability the way they want, without vendor lock-in.

We are growing fast and building core developer infra products.
And we are not fooling around:

 - 27,000+ GitHub stars

 - 800+ customers

 - 7,000+ members in our Slack community




ROLE: SR PRODUCT MANAGER - IC

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the product for a developer-infrastructure platform used by engineers every single day. This is a hands-on IC role: you'll go deep on the product surface, talk to power users constantly, and ship things that make complex observability workflows feel obvious. Our users are demanding, technical, and detail-driven — so you'll need to be too.




WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON

 - Alerts: Own the alerting experience end-to-end — rule creation, thresholds, anomaly detection, routing, and notifications — making it powerful for SREs while cutting alert fatigue through smarter grouping and signal-to-noise tuning, so on-call engineers trust what fires and land straight in the relevant data.

 - APM: Shape the application performance monitoring experience — service maps, latency/error/throughput views, and span analysis — and drive the "something's slow" → "here's the exact bottleneck" workflow that gets engineers to root cause fast.

 - Onboarding: Own the path from sign-up to first real value — instrumentation, first telemetry, first useful dashboard — reducing time-to-first-insight across language SDKs, collectors, and common frameworks, while respecting power users who want to skip the hand-holding.

 - Connected investigations: Define how alerts, APM, metrics, traces, and logs come together into a single coherent investigation rather than disconnected tabs, closing the loop from signal to root cause.

 - Observability UX: Sweat the details that matter to power users — query speed, sensible defaults, empty states, keyboard-driven workflows, the 50th query of the day — and make exploring high-cardinality, petabyte-scale data feel obvious rather than overwhelming.




WHAT WILL MAKE YOU SUCCESSFUL 

 - 5–8+ years in product management, with proven product work shipped at a B2B company

 - A track record of building product-centric, user-experience-led products — you're not just a backlog manager; you obsess over the actual experience

 - Deep attention to detail and high standards for power users — you sweat the empty states, the keyboard shortcuts, the defaults, the 50th query of the day, not just the demo path

 - Ability to drive initiatives end-to-end: problem discovery → definition → design → implementation → rollout → iteration

 - Strong technical fluency — you can read API docs, reason about data and systems, and earn the respect of senior engineers

 - Excellent written communication — clear PRDs, crisp tradeoff write-ups, and decisions documented for an async team

 - Comfortable in a high-ownership, fast-moving, remote-first environment
   
   


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Past experience in product team of a series B+ startup.

 - Experience in observability (monitoring / logging / tracing)

 - Familiarity with OpenTelemetry and/or ClickHouse, Kafka, Kubernetes, etc.

 - Has been, or wants to be, a founder in B2B/devtools
   
   


WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING AT SIGNOZ

 - Work on a globally used open-source project that engineers actually love

 - Huge scope and ownership – your work directly shapes how teams adopt SigNoz

 - Collaborate with high-caliber team who just can't stop shipping

 - Remote-first, async-friendly culture

 - Opportunity to help define the future of open-source observability

description:

Today we're at meaningful revenue scale with a finance setup that got us here but won't get us to the next stage. Our books are accurate but slow. We can tell you our blended gross margin — we can't yet tell you which customer cohorts, plans, and workloads are actually profitable. That matters more for us than for most SaaS companies: we run petabyte-scale infrastructure, so compute and storage cost per customer is our margin story.

You'll report to the CEO, own everything from monthly close to the due-diligence data room, and partner closely with engineering on the cost side of the business.

This is a build role. Real revenue, incomplete infrastructure, and you'll be constructing systems while the numbers keep moving.




WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Multi-entity finance across our US and India entities — intercompany, transfer pricing, consolidation

 - Compliance: GST, TDS, ROC/MCA, FEMA and RBI filings, ESOP administration and perquisite tax

 - Gross margin engineering: partnering with the platform team on infra spend, cloud commitments, and cost per ingested GB

 - FP&A: annual operating plan, rolling forecast built from operating drivers, MIS that functional leaders act on

 - Cash and treasury: 13-week cash flow, runway, USD/INR exposure, banking and surplus deployment

 - Working fluency in Indian startup compliance: GST, TDS, ROC, FEMA, ESOP taxation

 - Comfortable with messy, incomplete data and willing to ship a defensible answer before the data is perfect

 - Strong communication — can explain a margin problem to an engineer and a burn scenario to a board member in the same week

title: Founding Customer Success Lead
description:
WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

SigNoz is an open source observability platform built on OpenTelemetry: logs, metrics and traces in one tool. It's designed for an era where agents and humans run observability together. We are a YC company with 32K+ GitHub stars, and revenue grew 4x in 2025.

Most of our revenue is usage-based. That makes customer success especially important: retaining accounts and helping our larger accounts expand drive a big share of our growth.

This is our first dedicated customer success role. We're looking for a builder who can design the systems from scratch and set them up to scale as the team grows. You'll work directly with the founders.



WHAT YOU WILL OWN


1. ACCOUNT COVERAGE AND HEALTH

 - Tier our paying accounts and decide what each tier gets: a named owner, a shared Slack channel, regular business reviews, or pooled coverage.

 - Build health scores from data we already have in our warehouse: ingestion volume, product usage, billing, support tickets and engagement.

 - Set up a review cadence for the top tier, and make sure each top account has several contacts on their side, not one champion.


2. RETENTION AND SAVE PLAYS

 - Catch risk early. Usage drops, a champion leaving, a surprise bill and alerts going quiet are all signals. On a usage-based product, a billing spike can be as much of a churn risk as a usage drop.

 - Turn each signal into a play: who reaches out, what we offer (often help reducing their cost), and when it escalates.

 - Run a post-mortem on every meaningful churn or downgrade, and feed the lessons back into product, pricing and onboarding.

 - Run win-back campaigns for accounts we lost.


3. ANNUAL COMMITMENTS AND EXPANSION

 - Move monthly usage-based customers onto annual commitments, and own those conversations, including the commercial terms.

 - Spot expansion opportunities: new teams, new signals (logs, traces, metrics), new environments. Work with sales on the bigger ones.

 - Own renewals for customers on annual plans.


4. VOICE OF THE CUSTOMER

 - Bring what customers need back to product and engineering, ranked by revenue impact.

 - Work with our technical support team on escalations so the most important accounts never wait.


ACROSS ALL OF IT

 - Agree retention targets with the founders, then own the gross and net revenue retention numbers.

 - Run a weekly account review: at-risk accounts, saves, annual conversions in progress, expansion.


HOW THE ROLE GROWS

This role starts hands-on. You will personally own our top accounts and build the playbooks by running them yourself. We are not looking for someone who needs a team before anything happens.

Build the systems so they keep working as the number of accounts grows: clear tiers, health scores the team trusts, and playbooks a new CSM can pick up and run. Once they're working, you build and lead the customer success team.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - 30 days: You know the product and the data, and have met our top accounts. Account tiers and a first version of the health score are drafted.

 - 90 days: The health score is live and the team trusts it. Business reviews are running for the top tier. Save plays exist for usage drops and billing spikes, and every meaningful churn gets a post-mortem. The first monthly-to-annual conversions have closed.

 - 12 months: Gross and net revenue retention are measurably up, and a much larger share of revenue is on annual commitments. The systems you built are ready for the team to scale on.


WHO WE THINK FITS

 - 6-10 years in B2B SaaS customer success, with at least part of that at a technical product sold to engineers.

 - You've owned a revenue retention number (GRR, NRR or renewals), not just CSAT or ticket metrics. You can walk us through accounts you saved and grew, and what you did.

 - You've worked with usage-based or consumption pricing, and you know how to talk to a customer whose bill just jumped.

 - You're a builder. You've set up CS systems from scratch (health scores, business reviews, playbooks) and made them work as the book of accounts grew. You didn't just inherit them.

 - You're technical enough to talk to SREs and platform engineers, read a usage dashboard, and write basic SQL, or you'll learn it fast.

 - You're commercial. You can negotiate an annual commitment and you're comfortable talking about money.

 - You've managed US-based customers directly: running their reviews, handling escalations and negotiating renewals. You can overlap with US mornings (India evenings) a few times a week.

 - You've led or mentored other CSMs. Formal management is a plus, not a requirement.


BONUS POINTS

 - A background in engineering and can understand technical terms 

 - You've set up a CS platform or built health scoring on raw data

 - You've moved customers from monthly to annual plans at scale


WHY SIGNOZ

 - Customers who already love the product. Our customers chose us themselves. Your job is to keep that going as they grow, not to rescue bad deals.

 - Build the function from day one. You're the first dedicated CS hire, so you design how customer success works here and set it up to scale.

 - Work directly with the founders. You'll have the founders' backing, the data to work with, and a clear path to running the function.

 - A global dev-infra product, backed by YC and leading Bay Area VCs. Fully remote.

title: Product Manager - AI
description:
ABOUT SPOTDRAFT

SpotDraft is an AI-native contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform built for in-house legal teams “Draft, review, sign & renew faster, with legal in charge” The platform spans the full contract lifecycle: workflow-driven creation, negotiation and collaboration (across Word, Slack, and SpotDraft), a centralised repository with search and access controls, analytics, and native e-signatures compliant with ESIGN and eIDAS.

AI runs through the product, not beside it:

DraftMate AI turns documents into templates by auto-detecting placeholders.

Smart Data Capture extracts contract metadata so teams can search and report on any term.

VerifAI speeds up contract review inside Microsoft Word with suggestions, redlines, and automated compliance checks.

Sidebar is a team of always-on AI legal assistants (agents) that handle contract review against your playbooks, regulatory monitoring, and legal research, connected to your contract repository.

On-device AI runs VerifAI (embeddings, clause extraction, risk scoring, edits) entirely on Snapdragon processors, backed by a January 2026 Qualcomm Ventures round.

Customers include Abnormal Security, IPSY, Guideline, and Chaberton Energy, with a typical go-live in weeks rather than months. SpotDraft is venture-backed (Series A and Series B, plus a

January 2026 Qualcomm Ventures extension) and runs across Bengaluru and New York.



Top Outcomes:

Why this role exists

Our product roadmap increasingly depends on AI doing real work inside the product: extracting structured data from documents, and running agents that take action on a user’s behalf. That only works if two things are true: the underlying extraction is accurate enough to trust, and every AI action is governed (auditable, explainable, escalated to a human when it should be, and safely isolated between customers).

This role owns that platform. You turn “the AI isn’t accurate enough yet” and “agents need guardrails” into a roadmap, a trust bar, and an interface that other product teams can build against without a standing dependency on one engineer.




Day to Day:
Extraction accuracy

 - Own the roadmap to improve document/data extraction accuracy against defined targets, including major build-vs-improve calls on the underlying approach, in partnership with ML/engineering.

 - Define what "accurate enough to trust" means for each use case, and track progress against it on a live, shared metric.


Agent runtime & governance

 - Own product requirements for the runtime that lets AI agents take actions inside the product.

 - Own the governance layer: audit trail, explainability, human-in-the-loop escalation, policy enforcement, and tenant isolation. This is what makes an AI-driven action safe to ship, not just possible to build.

 - Define a policy-bounded interface for agent-triggered actions, so actions stay within defined guardrails without requiring engineering review per action.


Platform-as-a-service discipline

 - Define and maintain a self-serve interface so other product teams can build on this platform without filing a ticket to a single engineer for routine requests.

 - Partner with adjacent platform owners (e.g., core integrations/data) so teams building on top see one coherent surface, not competing conventions.

 - Push back on one-off requests that would turn the platform back into a bottleneck.



What success looks like (first 2-3 quarters)

 - A clear, evidence-based call made on the extraction approach, with a dated accuracy trajectory behind it rather than opinion.

 - Defined accuracy targets met on priority use cases, tracked on a live dashboard.

 - At least one AI-driven agent live in production with the escalation/governance loop actually working, not just the underlying model.

 - At least one other product team consuming the platform self-serve, with no standing ticket queue for routine requests.

 - Usage and override rates on agent-triggered actions instrumented and reviewed.
   



Requirements:

 - 3+ years in product management, including a stretch owning a platform, API, or infrastructure-facing product used by other internal teams, not exclusively customer-facing feature work.

 - Direct experience shipping ML/AI-backed product where trust and accuracy were the product, not a feature bullet. You’ve defined a precision/recall bar and held engineering to it.

 - Working fluency in what “governance” means for an AI system in production: audit trails, explainability, human-in-the-loop design, policy enforcement, tenant/data isolation. You don’t need to have built all of these, but you’ve shipped alongside at least one and know why each exists.

 - Comfortable owning a roadmap with genuine capability uncertainty and communicating that uncertainty honestly to stakeholders instead of smoothing it over.

 - Platform-PM instincts: default to “how do I make this self-serve” over “how do I build this feature for one team” Says no to scope creep that would make you a bottleneck.

 - Senior-level autonomy: given a problem area rather than a spec, you set the why, frame the what and how, and are trusted with the area’s roadmap and prioritization end to end.

Nice to have

 - Prior experience in a regulated domain where explainability/audit was a hard requirement rather than a nice-to-have.

 - Exposure to agent-action protocols (e.g., MCP) or policy-engine design for agentic systems.

Bonus points

None of these are required, but they will set you apart:

 - CLM, legal-tech, or contracts domain experience.

 - Direct customer-facing experience in a Sales, Customer Success, Solutions, or pre-sales role or a track record of close partnership with those teams.

 - Experience shipping AI-native or AI-assisted products to production.

 - A background in a fast-scaling B2B SaaS environment.

title: Principal Expert, US Insurance Industry
description:
LIFE AT UIPATH

The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.

Could that be you?



Your Mission:

UiPath is building a new way to design and deliver enterprise processes. UiPath cartographer draws on a curated library of industry process knowledge, interviews the business, and produces process maps and design documents. AI coding agents then turn those designs into working, orchestrated solutions, in days rather than months.

In insurance, "almost right" isn't good enough. The best AI companies in regulated industries have learned the same lesson: quality comes from making a senior practitioner part of the team to building the benchmarks, evaluations and feedback loops around their experience and judgment.

That's this role. As our Principal Expert for insurance, you will own the quality of everything our AI produces for US insurers. You'll set the bar, build the tests that hold the AI to it, and work in the field with customers and partners to make sure what we ship works in a real carrier.

This role does not carry a sales quota and is not a product management role. Success is measured by the quality of the insurance solutions we deliver and how confidently customers build on them.

Why this role is exciting:

 - Your work sets the standard. What you define as good will be used by insurance customers, partners and AI agents across the platform.

 - You see the impact. Take a process from discovery to a working solution in days, then keep improving it.

 - You're building something new. Help decide which lines of business we go after next and how we measure the success of AI-designed processes.



What you'll do at UiPath:

Own insurance AI quality

 - Own the quality of insurance process knowledge, designs and solutions across Property & Casualty and Life & Annuity.

 - Decide what needs fixing first, review changes before they go to customers, and sign off when a process is ready.

 - Work with industry experts, partners and reviewers to maintain and improve quality.

Build the insurance benchmark

 - Build a library of real insurance use cases covering claims, FNOL and triage, total loss, endorsements, life claims, medical records, disability claims and new business NIGO.

 - Define test cases, scoring criteria and expected answers to evaluate every new AI model and product release before it reaches customers.

Turn expert judgment into evaluations

 - Evaluate AI outputs at every stage, from process knowledge and process maps to design documents and working solutions.

 - Work with applied scientists and engineers to make sure automated AI evaluations match expert judgment, so we can scale quality checks without relying on manual reviews for everything.

Find failures and make sure they get fixed

 - Review actual outputs, identify common failure types across regulation, coverage, workflows, data and terminology, and prioritise them based on customer impact.

 - Turn recurring failures into reusable test cases and make sure fixes work before they go live.

 - Share clear updates on quality, key issues and progress with leadership, product teams and customers.



How you'll work:
You'll work in a small, senior team of automation consultants, engineers and applied scientists, working directly with customers.

 - Work with insurance carriers, MGAs and consulting partners to understand how their claims and underwriting teams operate, and test our designs against real processes.

 - Join consultants and engineers on customer deployments and use what you learn to improve our benchmarks and evaluations.

 - Run a regular review cycle, roughly every two weeks, to assess outputs, prioritise fixes and track improvements.

 - Join customer and partner meetings.



What you'll bring to the team:

 - Extensive experience (typically 12+ years) in US insurance, ideally starting hands-on in claims and moving into claims operations senior or mid level roles.

 - Deep P&C or Life & Annuity knowledge across the lifecycle

 - Working knowledge of US claims regulation: unfair claims settlement practices, state acknowledgment and payment deadlines, total-loss and salvage rules, and market conduct exams.

 - Experience mapping or redesigning claims or policy servicing operations: queues, handoffs, SLAs, exceptions, fraud referral and QA.

 - The confidence to review complex documents quickly, spot what's plausible but wrong, and explain exactly why.



Nice to have:

 - Life & Annuity or disability expertise: contestability, beneficiary determination, unclaimed property, suitability, and underwriting evidence such as medical records.

 - Experience evaluating AI or automation output: writing test cases, rubrics or reference answers, or running QA or validation programs.

 - Experience with insurance AI, claims automation or document intake programs.

 - Comfort with data and light technical work, such as spreadsheets, data analysis or prompting AI tools.

 - Experience leading or calibrating a team of reviewers, auditors or claims QA specialists.

 - Commercial lines, workers' compensation, employee benefits or broker/MGA experience.

description:
LIFE AT UIPATH

To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.

Your Mission:

Shape the future of agentic automation. UiPath is evolving from RPA to the world’s first Agentic Orchestration platform, enabling enterprises to deploy autonomous AI agents at scale. You’ll own one of the foundational layers that power it: Data Fabric and Ontology, the data and context layer that every other product on the platform (agents, workflows, and RPA) depends on to do its job. Your charter is to define where the data layer sits in the agentic stack, make it the obvious and trusted choice for developers and customers, and prove that value with real production adoption.

This is a high-agency, AI-native role. You won’t be running status meetings. You’ll be deep in the product: building agentic automations, prototyping with coding agents, talking with customers and FDEs, and turning what you learn into crisp direction for the engineers who build it.

The Platform You’ll Shape:

You’ll join the team building the foundational layers of UiPath’s agentic platform, the layers every agent, process, and workflow depends on. Data Fabric gives agents and workflows governed, real-time access to enterprise data. Ontology models those raw records into business entities and a connected semantic layer that automations can reason and act over. The work ahead: turning data into connected context agents can navigate, and making that context the backbone of how the platform reasons.

What You’ll Do at UiPath:

 - Own the strategy and positioning for UiPath’s data layer. Set the point of view on what the data layer is and why it matters in the agentic era. Turn that into the narrative leadership, marketing, and the field rally behind.

 - Own the vision and roadmap for Data Fabric and Ontology, making sharp tradeoff decisions on complex, ambiguous problems and proposing a clear path forward rather than just surfacing the ambiguity.

 - Drive adoption across every consuming surface. Partner with peer product and engineering teams to make Data Fabric and Ontology the default, and treat internal adoption as seriously as external demand.

 - Drive external go-to-market. Partner with marketing and sales on positioning, enablement, and demos; create demand and get your wins in front of the field and customers.

 - Be the customer’s champion. Engage directly in account conversations, get deep into real scenarios, and turn what you learn into validated use cases and roadmap decisions.

 - Own outcomes end to end. Take accountability from problem definition through launch, adoption, and the metrics that prove value: production adoption, breadth of connected data sources and entity coverage, consumption across platform surfaces, and query performance and trust.

 - Get technical. Work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering on design decisions, dogfood the product yourself, and stay credible on the underlying technology.

 - Make it agent-ready. Translate the fast-moving agent landscape (LLMs, coding agents, orchestration frameworks, MCP, evals) into a coherent UiPath point of view and a shipping product.

 - Raise the bar for the broader product team through thought leadership, a strong point of view in forums, and mentoring, setting the standard for how the platform thinks about data and context.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

 - 8+ years of product management on technical, platform, or developer products, ideally in B2B SaaS or enterprise software.

 - Data and semantic depth. Hands-on experience with data platforms and with modeling business objects as entities; familiarity with semantic layers, knowledge graphs, or ontologies is a strong advantage.

 - A builder’s instinct. You’ve shipped infrastructure that other builders rely on, and you’d rather prototype and dogfood than write a spec and wait.

 - Technical depth. You go deep on technical design with engineering and are comfortable in the product yourself, not just managing from the roadmap.

 - Hands-on with AI, not conceptual. You have built or integrated AI/ML into live products yourself, and you use LLM-based tools (copilots, coding agents, prototyping tools) in your own daily work.

 - A strategic narrative. You can define a category and a point of view, and tell a clear “why now” and “why us” story that executives, the field, and customers buy into.

 - A genuine customer-champion mindset. You seek out direct customer conversations and let real scenarios drive what you build.

 - GTM drive. You’ve created demand and driven adoption, not just delivered features

 - Crisp, decision-rich communication and the ability to influence across engineering, design, sales, and marketing without authority.

 - Bias to ownership and action. You take ambiguous, high-stakes problems and drive them to a result with minimal direction.

 - Customer engagement: Work directly with finance leaders and process owners at large US enterprises to understand their operations, validate process maps, identify improvement opportunities and support the development of relevant use cases.

 - Process knowledge development: Build and maintain finance process knowledge, creating reusable process maps, business rules, exception catalogues, KPIs and

 - industry best practices.

WHAT YOU'LL DO AT UIPATH

1. Product validation and process expertise

 - Test UiPath finance solutions against real-world finance processes, using customer documentation, SOPs, process recordings, system workflows and SME interviews.

 - Review and validate AS-IS and TO-BE process maps, ensuring they accurately reflect how work is performed across finance teams.

 - Challenge AI-generated outputs, identifying missing steps, incorrect business rules, overlooked exceptions and assumptions that do not reflect actual business practices.

 - Validate process design documents (PDDs), solution design documents (SDDs), business rules and decision logic.

 - Develop reference process maps and test scenarios with expected outcomes for the different O2C processes.

 - Work closely with product and engineering teams to provide structured feedback and improve UiPath’s ability to understand and document finance processes.

 - Work with our engineering team to design, configure and build AI finance solutions that work in the real world.

 - Ensure that the solutions being developed reflect the decisions, controls and judgement that experienced finance professionals would apply.

2. Customer engagement and use-case development

 - Lead process discovery workshops and interviews with CFOs, Controllers, VPs of Accounts Receivable, Credit Directors and other finance process owners.

 - Work with selected design partners and enterprise customers to understand their existing processes, operating models, systems and challenges.

 - Validate solution outputs with customer SMEs and ensure that the documented processes reflect actual business operations.

 - Identify opportunities to improve finance operations through automation, AI agents and orchestration.

 - Translate customer problems into clearly defined use cases, process requirements and measurable business outcomes.

 - Help customers understand the potential impact of automation through relevant KPIs such as DSO, cash application rates, deduction recovery rates, order cycle times and invoice accuracy.

 - Support the sales and vertical solutions teams in customer conversations, particularly when discussing finance processes, transformation opportunities and business value.

 - Bring customer feedback and emerging requirements back to product and engineering teams.

3. Process Atlas and finance knowledge development

 - Build and maintain oCFO process knowledge within UiPath.

 - Develop structured process maps covering process stages, activities, roles, systems, data, business rules, decision points and exceptions.

 - Document industry-specific variations and common exceptions across different finance operating models.

 - Develop reusable business rules, decision tables, exception catalogues and worked examples that can be used by AI agents.

 - Define standard KPIs, performance measures and relevant industry benchmarks for each process.

 - Ensure that the knowledge base reflects both standard operating procedures and the practical judgement used by experienced finance professionals.

 - Maintain the quality and accuracy of UiPath’s process knowledge library as customer feedback, product changes and operational learnings emerge.

Finance and Order-to-Cash experience

 - Strong hands-on experience managing or leading Accounts Receivable, Credit Management, Collections or broader O2C operations.

   - Credit Management
   
   - Order Management
   
   - Billing and Invoicing
   
   - Collections and Dunning
   
   - Deductions and Disputes
   
   - Cash Application

 - Strong understanding of US B2B finance operations, including retailer deductions, trade promotions, lockbox processing, ACH remittance, EDI transactions, US sales tax and SOX controls.

 - Experience working with finance transformation, shared services or global business services teams.

 - Understanding of the relationship between O2C, working capital, treasury and financial reporting.

Process transformation and documentation

 - Ability to develop detailed AS-IS and TO-BE process maps, process definition documents, business requirements and operating procedures.

 - Ability to translate complex business processes into clear business rules, decision logic and exception-handling procedures.

Enterprise systems and technology

 - Working knowledge of major ERP platforms such as SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Fusion, Oracle EBS, NetSuite or Microsoft Dynamics 365.

 - Experience with at least one finance or AR automation platform such as HighRadius, Billtrust, Esker, Serrala, Versapay or Emagia.

 - Understanding of how finance processes operate across ERP, CRM, billing, banking and customer-facing systems.

Customer and communication skills

 - Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to engage confidently with senior finance stakeholders.

 - Ability to explain complex finance processes in a simple and structured manner.

 - Strong documentation and writing skills, particularly when converting business knowledge into reusable process documentation.

 - Comfortable working across product, engineering, consulting and go-to-market teams.

 - Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities and take ownership of the quality of functional deliverables.

title: Principal Product Manager, Enterprise Governance
description:
LIFE AT UIPATH

The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.

Could that be you?




YOUR MISSION

We're seeking a Principal Product Manager to join our Governance team. You'll drive product direction across human, robot, and agent identity, delegated and scoped authorization, guardrails, and audit and attribution for non-human actors, and you'll work the patterns the industry is still standardizing right now: on-behalf-of delegation chains, OAuth flows for autonomous callers, just-in-time elevation, sandboxing, and policy-as-code for tool access.

This is a high-agency, AI-native role. You will be deep in the product: testing, prototyping with coding agents, talking to customers, and turning what you learn into a coherent roadmap to build.

Your north star is an agentic enterprise’ trust translating into adoption: governance with required coverage, and monitoring, for enterprises; and frictionless for builders to code it in.




WHAT YOU'LL DO AT UIPATH

 - Own the 12–18 months roadmap for identity, auth, and access governance across UiPath's agentic platform, in coherence with company priorities and evolving standards in the ecosystem.

 - Evolve how identity works for agents, robots, and humans at UiPath (provisioning, scoping, delegation, attestation), ship the patterns, and drive their adoption across the product teams that build on them.

 - Drive the auth model for LLM tool-calling (for internal and external agents),  enterprise-managed authorization, scoped consent, least-privilege execution, step-up and just-in-time elevation, and OOTB monitoring views, audit trails that hold up in front of a compliance team.

 - Enhance the guardrail layer around agent action: policy-as-code for tool access, sandboxing boundaries, approval and elevation flows, and the attribution model that answers "which agent, on whose behalf, under which policy" after the fact.

 - Define how UiPath agents present themselves to the outside world and how outside agents present themselves to UiPath: agent identities registered in enterprise directories, on-behalf-of delegation chains that survive multiple hops, and agent-to-agent trust.

 - Partner with our largest and most regulated customers (financial services, healthcare, public sector) on production deployments. Go deep enough to know which specific control failed and ship the fix.

 - Use the platform as a builder. Stand up agents, wire up auth flows, use coding agents aggressively to prototype and ship reference implementations.

 - Instrument and own the metrics that matter (e.g. time-to-grant, audit coverage, policy violations caught, developer friction) and prioritize against them.

 - Present UiPath's governance capabilities and roadmap to customers, partners, and consider authoring any external content that earns CISO trust.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TEAM

 - 7+ years in technical PM or engineering roles, with sustained time in the governance space: identity, access, and guardrails for enterprise software. You have shipped infrastructure that enterprises trusted with production traffic.

 - A visible record of innovating in agentic governance specifically: owned capabilities, reference implementations, spec or working-group contributions.

 - Fluency in enterprise identity and access: how users, services, and now agents authenticate, what they're allowed to do, and how actions get audited.

 - Working knowledge of the agent auth stack as it stands today: MCP authorization, on-behalf-of delegation, and how IdPs like Okta and Entra now model agents as identities.

 - Working understanding of agentic AI (tool-calling, MCP, RAG, agent design patterns) and a view on how identity, access, and guardrails should evolve to support autonomous actors.

 - First-principles thinker, comfortable in ambiguity. Can produce a defensible direction and can tell the difference between a problem the standards will solve for us.

 - Clear communicator, in writing and in person: you can write a short position doc that frames a decision, explain a concept well to a CISO or auditor, and walk a customer through a working demo without overselling it.




IDEAL BACKGROUND

 - Several years in identity, access, or security-platform product work in enterprise vendors - hyperscaler identity team, IAM vendors, workload-identity or secrets vendor, or as an early PM at a startup in the space, with focus on agents.

We are building an immersive feed inside the Meesho app, focused on look-based, trend-based, and highly personalized inspiration across major lifestyle categories like Fashion, Home, and Beauty.
The DAU Labs team focuses on building engaging discovery experiences, scaling content supply, and solving complex personalization and ranking problems to drive user engagement, daily active users (DAU), and long-term retention.
About the Role
As a Product Manager II at DAU Labs, you will play a key role in building and scaling Meesho's content-led discovery experience. You will work on creating engaging and personalized product experiences that help millions of users discover relevant trends, products, and inspiration.
You will own key product problems across content discovery, personalization, user engagement, and conversion. Working closely with Engineering, Data Science, Design, and Business teams, you will identify opportunities, drive product improvements, and deliver measurable impact on DAU growth and user retention.


What you will do
•
Product Strategy & Ownership: Own key product areas within the content discovery ecosystem, identify user and business problems, and define product roadmaps aligned with DAU growth objectives.

•
Discovery & Personalization: Work on improving content discovery, feed relevance, recommendation systems, and personalization to deliver engaging experiences tailored to different user cohorts.

•
User Engagement & Growth: Identify opportunities to improve user engagement, daily active usage, session frequency, and long-term retention through data-driven product initiatives.

•
Experimentation & Analytics: Drive product experiments, A/B testing, and data analysis to identify growth opportunities, measure product performance, and continuously improve user experience.

•
Product Execution: Work closely with Engineering, Design, and Data Science teams to translate business problems into product requirements and drive end-to-end execution.

•
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Content, Category Marketing, Seller Experience, and other business teams to improve content quality, discovery, and content-to-commerce conversion.

•
0-to-1 Problem Solving: Identify new opportunities, solve ambiguous product problems, and build scalable product solutions that create meaningful user and business impact

What you will need 
•
Experience: Overall experience of 4+ years, with at least 4+ years of experience in Product Management in a tech-led company. Experience in B2C or consumer internet companies is preferred.

•
Product & Domain Expertise: Experience working on consumer-facing products, content-led platforms, discovery experiences, recommendation systems, personalization, or engagement-focused products is preferred.

•
Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills: Strong analytical aptitude with the ability to solve complex and ambiguous problems related to user discovery, engagement, personalization, and product growth.

•
Execution Bias: Strong bias for action and execution, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver outcomes in a fast-paced environment.

•
Data-Driven Mindset: Ability to use data, user insights, and experimentation to identify opportunities, make product decisions, and measure outcomes.

•
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work effectively with Engineering, Design, Data Science, and Business teams to drive product initiatives end to end.

•
Mindset: Strong passion for Problem First Solving (PFS), ownership, and building scalable products from 0 to 1.

Democratising internet commerce for everyone — Meesho (Meri Shop) started with a single idea in mind: to be an e-commerce destination for Indian consumers and to enable small businesses to succeed online.

About Zeta

At Zeta tech innovation is married with exceptional design. We are crafting the best Digital Banking Experiences for the largest financial institutions across the globe encompassing credit cards, commercial credit, deposits, loans, family banking and other financial products and services.

Our Product Design Philosophies

Delight through Design

At Zeta we believe in meticulously crafting digital experiences with delight as a central focus. This philosophy goes beyond mere functionality; it aims to evoke ecstasy in users. The key is to create an emotional connection between the user and the product, transforming routine interactions into memorable experiences. This involves a deep understanding of the product and the user's needs, desires, and pain points, leveraging color, typography, layout to elicit emotion, pleasure and surprise.

Outcome driven UX

"Outcome-Driven UX" is a design philosophy that extends UX beyond the traditional goals of usability and aesthetic appeal, focusing on explicitly achieving tangible, measurable results such as improving funnel conversion rates, retention, and revenue generation. Every design decision is guided by how it can positively impact these metrics. The user interface and experience are meticulously crafted to not only be user-friendly but also to strategically influence user behavior in a way that contributes directly to the company's overall success. This entails an in depth understanding of the business objectives; rigorous analysis of user behavior; rapid iterative Experimentation leveraging intuition and experience, and data driven decisions.

title: Senior Product Manager - Core Product Experience
description:
InMobi (Corporate)

InMobi Group is a global technology company shaping the future of agentic commerce and advertising. Through its ecosystem of businesses — including InMobi Advertising and flagship consumer platform Glance — InMobi leverages data, machine learning, and generative AI to help brands reach audiences more precisely and consumers discover products more intuitively. Glance, which is pioneering new models of agentic commerce, is owned and operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of InMobi Pte. Ltd.

InMobi Advertising

InMobi Advertising, part of global technology company InMobi, is an agentic advertising platform helping brands and merchants achieve their business outcomes. Through its proprietary intelligence, AI-led solutions, and vast consumer reach — including flagship consumer platform Glance — InMobi Advertising delivers the omnichannel performance defining what's next in advertising and commerce. Glance is owned and operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of InMobi Pte. Ltd. To learn more, visit advertising.inmobi.com.

Glance

Glance is an intelligent shopping agent, redefining the commerce experience. Powered by proprietary agentic intelligence and generative AI, Glance delivers a hyper-personalized consumer experience across mobile and TV — shaping the new era of shopping. Glance is operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of global technology leader InMobi, and is backed by Mithril Capital, Google and Jio Platforms. To learn more, visit glance.com.

About Accelerate:
Accelerate is InMobi’s AI-native, self-serve campaign management platform for SMBs, D2C brands, agencies and enterprise advertisers. An advertiser describes their brand and goals; Accelerate’s agents plan, create, launch and optimize campaigns across ad platforms such as TikTok and OpenAI, with more supply integrations on the way.
We are building toward a fully autonomous marketing platform. This role sits on the demand side, reporting to the Group Product Manager for Customer Experience Core.

About the role:
You will own the heart of Accelerate: the experience that turns a brand’s goals into a live, running campaign. That includes campaign creation, the chat interface advertisers use to work with our agents, and AI creative generation. You will make that one experience work for very different customers: an SMB owner launching a first campaign, an agency running dozens of client accounts, a mid-size advertiser scaling spend, and an enterprise team with approval processes. You will also take Accelerate beyond our own
app, through APIs for companies that want our capabilities without onboarding, and through bundled offerings inside SMB-heavy platforms such as Stripe, Razorpay and Shopify. This is a senior, high-ownership role. The product is agentic and LLM-driven, so you will shape not just screens but how the agent reasons, what it produces, and how we measure whether it is good.

What you will own:

• Campaign creation, chat and creative generation. The hero surface where an advertiser’s brand blueprint becomes a live campaign. You own the end-to-end flow, the conversation design, and the quality of what the agent produces.

• Segment-specific journeys. One product that adapts to SMBs, agencies, mid-size advertisers and enterprise clients. Includes multi-account workflows for agencies and controls, approvals and roles for enterprise.

• AI quality for your surfaces. Prompt and RAG design for brand context, eval sets that define “good” for a campaign plan or a creative, and quality gates that releases must pass. The Agentic AI pod owns platform-wide autonomy tiers and guardrails; you own whether your surfaces produce the right output.

• APIs and headless access. A public API so partners and larger customers can create and manage campaigns without using our UI. You own the developer experience, docs and pricing model, working with engineering on the design.

• Embedded distribution. Accelerate as a bundled offering inside platforms such as Stripe, Razorpay and Shopify. You shape the product side of these partnerships: the in-partner experience, account linking and the value proposition, working with the business team on the deals.

• Metrics. Time from brief to live campaign, campaign launch rate, creative acceptance rate, eval pass rates, and adoption by segment and by channel (app, API, partner).

What we’re looking for:

• 6+ years of product management, with at least 2 years owning a B2B product used by multiple customer segments.

• You have shipped an LLM-powered product to real users in production, not just a pilot or demo. You have dealt with hallucinations, latency, cost and quality regressions.

• Hands-on understanding of RAG, prompt design, agentic workflows and evals. You have written eval sets yourself and used them to decide whether something ships.

• Strong design sense. You can show work where you shaped the experience in detail, and you partner with designers as a peer.

• You work AI-native (see “How we work” below). You prototype, write and reason with LLMs as part of your daily work.

• Comfortable with ambiguity and a wide scope. You can keep the hero surface moving while building the API and partnership tracks alongside it.

• Clear written communication with engineers, designers, business partners and customers.

Strong pluses

• Experience in martech, adtech or performance marketing products, or time as a performance marketer yourself.

• Built or owned a public API, developer platform or partner app (for example, a Shopify app or a payment-platform integration).

• Shipped a product that serves both self-serve SMBs and enterprise or agency accounts from one codebase.

• Experience with generative creative: image, video or ad copy generation with brand-safety checks.

• A portfolio or public writing showing your product and design thinking.

How we work
Accelerate is an AI-native product, and we build it the AI-native way. Every PM on the demand side is expected to:

• Prototype before you spec. Turn an idea into a clickable prototype with AI tools in hours, and test it with users and the team before writing requirements.

• Write and think with LLMs. Draft PRDs, edge cases, test cases, and analyses with an LLM as a working partner. Then apply your own judgment to what it gets wrong.

• Hand off with less back-and-forth. Give engineering and design specs precise enough to build from, with prototypes and acceptance criteria attached, so fewer decisions get made in meetings.

• Stay close to the data. Pull and analyze data yourself rather than waiting on a dashboard request.

• Bring design sense. Care about the details of the customer experience and partner with design as a peer, not a requester. We will test this in the interview loop, not just ask about it.

Since 2007, InMobi has built the extraordinary. Beyond just technology. It has built a way of working.

Across 16 offices globally, through every pivot and breakthrough, one thing has remained constant: we are builders, dreamers, doers. We are fluid enough to move fast, grounded enough to own outcomes, and human enough to care deeply about the work and about one another.

Culture is at the core of that ethos. It has been co-created by the people who built this company and by those continuing to shape it every day. It lives in how we work, how decisions are made, how teams show up for one another, and how seriously we take the responsibility to build the best.

This is a place where ambition and belonging occupy the same space. Where the bar is high and the support is real. Where freedom comes with trust, and trust comes with accountability. Where you are valued not only for what you do, but for the perspective, judgment and humanity you bring to the work. Where you will be challenged by the work and supported by the communities, passions and experiences that shape who you are beyond your role.

If this sounds like the place you have been looking for, join us.

Find out more here: InMobi Culture

About Accelerate:
Accelerate is InMobi’s AI-native, self-serve campaign management platform for SMBs, D2C brands, agencies and enterprise advertisers. An advertiser describes their brand and goals; Accelerate’s agents plan, create, launch and optimize campaigns across ad platforms such as TikTok and OpenAI, with more supply integrations on the way.
We are building toward a fully autonomous marketing platform. The product team is organized by capability, not segment. This role sits on the demand side, reporting to the Group Product Manager, alongside Customer Experience Core (campaign creation, onboarding and activation).

About the role:
You will build Accelerate’s payments and money infrastructure from zero. Every dollar or rupee an advertiser puts into Accelerate flows through what you build: how they fund their account, how spend is drawn down across ad platforms, how they are invoiced, refunded and taxed, and how we settle with suppliers.
There is no legacy system to inherit. You will define the wallet, the ledger behind it, and the integration with our third-party payments partner (Vyre), then own the revenue metrics that depend on them. Getting this right is what lets an SMB go from signup to live campaign in minutes, and what lets finance trust every number on the dashboard.
You will work with a Senior Product Associate on the pod, engineering, Central Design, and InMobi finance, tax and legal teams.

What you will own:

• Advertiser wallet. A prepaid balance advertisers top up and Accelerate draws down as campaigns spend. Includes funding methods, auto-recharge, low-balance alerts, credit lines for larger accounts, and the rules for how a balance can and cannot be used.

• Ledger and reconciliation. The source of truth for every credit, debit, hold, refund and adjustment. Spend reported by each ad platform must reconcile to the ledger, with clear handling for mismatches.

• Payments integration. End-to-end integration with Vyre, our third-party payments partner: collections, payment methods, failures and retries, webhooks, and the fallback plan if a provider is down.

• Billing, invoicing and tax. Invoices, receipts, GST, TDS on ad spend, and multi-currency handling as we add international advertisers.

• Supplier settlement. How we pay out and reconcile with ad platforms, working with the business team that handles supplier contracts.

• Segment needs. SMBs prepaying by card or UPI, agencies funding many client accounts from one place, and enterprise clients on invoiced terms.

• Revenue metrics. Top-up conversion, payment success rate, time to first funded campaign, wallet balance retention, and reconciliation accuracy. Every revenue number in Accelerate’s success framework depends on your system.

What we’re looking for:

• 6+ years of product management, with at least 3 years owning payments, wallets, billing or ledger systems.

Strong pluses

• Experience with ad-platform billing (prepaid, postpaid or credit-line models) or marketplace payouts.

How we work:
Accelerate is an AI-native product, and we build it the AI-native way. Every PM on the demand side is expected to:

title: Associate Director, Risk Management
description:
Razorpay is one of India’s leading full-stack financial technology companies, powering the way businesses move, manage, and grow money. Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar with a simple vision - to simplify payments for Indian businesses - we’ve since grown into a fintech powerhouse driving India’s digital payment revolution.

Razorpay powers millions of businesses with a smarter, scalable stack that goes beyond transactions to help them truly build and grow.

From building AI-native agentic payments, to AI-assisted fraud detection and real-time risk intelligence to automated reconciliation, smart payouts, and predictive financial insights, we are embedding intelligence across our stack to make money movement faster, safer, and more efficient. In close collaboration with ecosystem partners - including banks, networks, regulators - we are pioneering industry-first solutions that are shaping the next era of fintech

Across India, Singapore and Malaysia, our products span everything from seamless checkouts to payroll automation - powering a fintech ecosystem that’s redefining how money moves across Asia.

Today, that ecosystem supports everyone from early-stage startups to some of India’s largest enterprises, enabling them to accept, process, and disburse payments at scale while expanding into new ways of managing money more efficiently.

Our scale speaks volumes: Razorpay processes $180+ billion in annualized transactions, powering leading businesses like Airbnb, Facebook, WhatsApp, Airtel, CRED, BookmyShow, Zomato, Swiggy, Lenskart, Mirae Asset Capital markets, Indian Oil, National Pension Scheme - and over 100 of India’s unicorns. With strong roots in India and growing operations in Southeast Asia, we are shaping the next chapter of financial technology across the region.

We are backed by global investors including GIC, Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India & SEA), Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, MasterCard, and Salesforce Ventures, having raised over $740 million to date. Strategic acquisitions - including Ezetap (POS and offline payments), Curlec (Malaysia expansion), BillMe (digital invoicing), and POP (rewards-first UPI) - along with earlier moves in fraud prevention, payroll, and lending, have further strengthened our platform and widened our footprint across Asia.

But what truly sets Razorpay apart is our culture. At Razorpay, ownership is our oxygen - you own what you build, with no micromanagement or red tape, just the runway to make your ideas fly. Learning is a lifestyle - if you’re curious, you’ll feel at home here. People > Pedigree - we hire for attitude, hustle, and hunger more than degrees. Transparency thrives over titles - this is where interns question CXOs and CXOs say “thank you.” Guided by our values of Customer First, Autonomy & Ownership, Agility with Integrity, Transparency, Challenging the status quo and a strong belief that Razorpay grows with Razors, you’ll be part of a 3000+ strong team building not just products, but the financial infrastructure of the future.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a senior risk leader to build and oversee the entire risk monitoring program for our international expansion, spanning the United States, Singapore, Malaysia, and upcoming regions. This is a strategic and operational leadership role — you will own the design of the multi-region monitoring framework, lead and scale the teams that run it, and serve as the senior risk voice in expansion decisions.

Reporting into senior leadership, you will be accountable for ensuring that as we enter each new market, our AML, transaction monitoring, merchant risk, and fraud capabilities are not just compliant with local regulation but operationally excellent — rule sets tuned to local typologies, alert quality high, investigation cycles fast, and regulators and partners confident in our program.

The ideal candidate combines deep payments/fintech financial-crime expertise with genuine program-building experience: you have stood up monitoring functions in new geographies, hired and grown teams, selected and implemented tooling, and translated regulatory expectations into working controls.

This role requires close collaboration with Compliance, Legal, Product, Operations, Data Science, Engineering, and external stakeholders including regulators, acquiring banks, networks, and law enforcement across jurisdictions.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Multi-Region Risk Monitoring Strategy & Program Ownership

•
Own the end-to-end risk monitoring program for international markets — current and upcoming — covering AML/CFT transaction monitoring, fraud detection, chargeback abuse, and merchant portfolio risk.

•
Design the market-entry risk framework: regulatory landscape assessment, typology research, rule/scenario design, threshold calibration, and phased go-live plans for each new region.

•
Set the multi-year roadmap for the program: coverage gaps, automation opportunities, analytics maturity, and headcount/tooling investment cases.

•
Define and own program-level KRIs/KPIs — alert volumes, false positive ratios, time-to-disposition, STR throughput, loss rates — and report regularly to senior management and board-level stakeholders.

2. Regulatory Alignment Across Jurisdictions

•
Ensure the monitoring program meets local requirements across US (FinCEN/BSA, OFAC sanctions, state money transmitter expectations), Singapore (MAS Notice 626/PSN02), Malaysia (BNM AML/CFT policy documents), and each upcoming market.

•
Partner with Compliance and Legal on regulatory examinations, audits, and information requests in each region; represent the risk monitoring program to regulators where required.

•
Anticipate regulatory change across jurisdictions and adapt frameworks proactively rather than reactively.

•
Drive alignment between international program standards and the parent program so global consistency and local specificity are both preserved.

3. Team Leadership & Capability Building

•
Build, lead, and mentor regional risk monitoring and investigations teams (analysts, team leads, and future regional heads), with hiring plans that scale with market expansion.

•
Establish operating rhythms — quality assurance programs, calibration sessions, case review standards, training curricula — that raise the floor of investigative quality across all regions.

•
Develop succession depth and specialist capability (sanctions, mule networks, merchant collusion, emerging typologies).

•
Champion a culture of intellectual honesty: investigations that follow evidence, escalations without fear, and post-mortems without blame.

4. Analytics, Tooling & Automation Strategy

•
Own the vision for analytics-led monitoring: rules-plus-models architecture, ML-based alert scoring, network/graph analytics for mule and collusion detection.

•
Drive build-vs-buy decisions and vendor/tooling selection (TM platforms, case management, KYC/EDD data providers, sanctions screening) in partnership with Engineering and Procurement.

•
Set data quality standards for monitoring — transaction enrichment, merchant metadata, watchlists — and partner with Data teams to close gaps.

•
Establish A/B testing and champion-challenger discipline for rule and model changes so monitoring improves measurably over time.

5. Merchant & Portfolio Risk Oversight

•
Oversee post-onboarding merchant risk programs across regions: ongoing monitoring, periodic reviews, enhanced due diligence for high-risk categories, and business model verification.

•
Investigate and resolve portfolio-level anomalies — chargeback spikes, abnormal payment patterns, transaction laundering, misuse of payment services — and drive control changes with Product and Ops.

•
Advise on risk appetite for new verticals, products, and markets before launch; ensure restricted/high-risk business categories have proportionate controls in every region.

6. Cross-Functional & External Stakeholder Leadership

•
Act as the senior risk counterpart to regional business leadership for expansion decisions — new products, partnerships, and market entries get a rigorous but constructive risk assessment.

•
Manage relationships with acquiring banks, networks, regulators, law enforcement, and external partners across all operating regions.

•
Represent Risk in cross-functional governance forums; influence without authority across Product, Engineering, and regional ops teams.

•
Train and upskill internal teams across regions on AML risks, suspicious activity identification, and fraud prevention.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

•
Experience: 10–12 years in AML, transaction monitoring, financial crime risk, merchant risk, or fraud within payments, fintech, card networks, banking, or e-money institutions.

•
People Leadership: 5+ years of people leadership, including building or substantially scaling teams; experience hiring and developing regional leads preferred.

•
International Regulatory Experience: Direct experience operating in at least one of: US, Singapore, or Malaysia regulatory environments — working knowledge of FinCEN/OFAC, MAS, and BNM expectations, and demonstrated ability to learn new jurisdictions quickly.

•
Program Building: Proven track record of building or transforming a monitoring program — not just running one: market entry, tooling selection/implementation, rule/scenario design, or analytics transformation.

•
Technical Expertise: Strong grasp of TM platforms and case management systems; comfortable shaping architecture decisions with Engineering.

•
Investigative Skills: Strong investigative instincts: able to identify anomalies, connect data points, and build defensible narratives; equally able to review others' work and raise its quality.

•
Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication — able to write for regulators, present to executives, and explain risk trade-offs to product teams.

•
Education & Certifications: Bachelor's degree in finance, law, data, or related field; ACAMS (CAMS), ICA, or CFCS certifications strongly preferred; advanced degrees a plus.

WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE COMPELLING

•
Ownership, not stewardship: You define what the international risk monitoring program becomes — its architecture, its team, its reputation with regulators.

•
Multi-region canvas: US, SG, MY live today; more regions coming — your framework sets the pattern for every future market.

•
Senior visibility: Direct line to senior leadership, and a seat at the table for every major expansion decision.

•
Build with support: A proven parent program in India, strong Data/Engineering partners, and leadership that treats risk as a growth enabler, not a brake.

Razorpay believes in and follows an equal employment opportunity policy that doesn't discriminate on gender, religion, sexual orientation, colour, nationality, age, etc. We welcome interests and applications from all groups and communities across the globe.

Follow us on LinkedIn & Twitter
